results.title: Animals backend
results.summary: I reviewed all of origin/main...HEAD in trade-imports-animals-backend (PR #107, 4 commits). I also followed the new status downstream into the outbox, trade-imports-dynamics-gateway, trade-imports-ins-backend and the GBN-AG schemas in trade-imports-schemas. Inside the service the change holds up: status guards, null handling on cancel-amend for older records, the projection fields and the unit coverage are all sound. The serious problem is the wire contract. Every submit without a scanned ITAHC now sends notificationStatusCode SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED to PIMS on events whose declared schemas pin it to the constant SUBMITTED, and trade-imports-schemas was not changed. A second, medium defect: cancel-amend restores a stored status that can disagree with the documents actually held.
results.answersCheck: The reviewer answered no explicit questions. Two points in the summary need tightening. First, the reviewer says the new status goes out on 'every submit without a scanned ITAHC'. It is broader than that: an ITAHC uploaded but still at scan PENDING at submit also produces SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED, and nothing re-evaluates the status when the scan later completes. That makes the wire-contract exposure in f1 more common, not less. Second, Sam's ruling of 2026-10-09, point 8, says explicitly that no PIMS profile or trade-imports-schemas change is made in this programme. That supports f1: the build should have kept the GBN-AG wire value at SUBMITTED, so Option 1 of the suggested fix (map to SUBMITTED on the wire) is the one that fits Sam's rulings. Apart from that I agree with the summary.

survived.title: SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED sent to PIMS on events whose schemas require SUBMITTED
survived.what: submitNotification and cancelAmendNotification now write the aggregate with status SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED. OutboxService then serialises it unchanged into two places: data.exchangedDocument.notificationStatusCode (through ExchangedDocument.from, status.name()) and statusChanges[].status. The events are NotificationSubmitted, NotificationSubmissionAmended and NotificationAmendmentCancelled, and each carries a schemaUrl. The schemas those URLs name all pin the value with {"const": "SUBMITTED"}: trade-imports-schemas gbn-ag-event-notification-submitted-v1, -submission-amended-v1 and -amendment-cancelled-v1. The GBN-AG status codelist (codelists/gbn-ag-notification-status.json) and gbn-ag-state-transitions.md know only DRAFT, SUBMITTED, AMEND and DELETED. trade-imports-schemas is still on main and has no change for the new status. The dynamics gateway passes the string straight through to PIMS (PimsGbnAgDataMapper/V2 pass doc.notificationStatusCode() through; OutboxStatusChange.status is a String). Sam's add-only ruling (claim 42) mapped the new status in the animals frontend and the INS frontend, but not in the external GBN-AG/PIMS contract. NotificationIT line 938 now pins the non-conforming value as expected behaviour, and four older outbox ITs were changed from SUBMITTED to SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED.
survived.scenario: A trader submits a live-animals notification without a scanned ITAHC. The ITs show this is now the default for any notification with no document. The outbox writes a NotificationSubmitted event that declares schemaUrl gbn-ag-event-notification-submitted-v1.schema.json but carries notificationStatusCode "SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED". The gateway forwards it to PIMS over Azure Service Bus. PIMS either fails schema validation, or does not recognise the code and does not treat the notification as submitted. The BCP and caseworkers then never see a pre-notification the trader believes was submitted. Each later amend, cancel-amend or resubmit repeats the problem.
survived.fix: Do not ship until the wire contract is settled. Option 1: keep the GBN-AG wire status as SUBMITTED by mapping SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED to SUBMITTED in ExchangedDocument.from and when building StatusChange. Carry the outstanding items as their own field if downstream needs them; this also means the INS backend (NotificationUpsertService reads status only from notificationStatusCode) needs another way to show 'action required'. Option 2: add the code to the gbn-ag codelist and minted v2 event schemas in trade-imports-schemas, agreed with the PIMS team, on the same branch name. Either way, add an IT asserting a clean-ITAHC submit's event carries notificationStatusCode SUBMITTED.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed on the branch. NotificationStatus gains SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED (diff). submitNotification (NotificationService.java:202-212) uses it whenever OutstandingItem.outstandingFor finds no COMPLETE ITAHC or HEALTH_CERTIFICATE. That covers no upload and also an ITAHC whose scan is still PENDING at submit. cancelAmendNotification (line 288) can restore it too. ExchangedDocument.from (outbox/gbnag/ExchangedDocument.java:32) writes status.name() into notificationStatusCode, and OutboxService:74-76 appends it to statusChanges. OutboxEventType points the schemaUrl at gbn-ag-event-notification-submitted-v1, -submission-amended-v1 and -amendment-cancelled-v1. In trade-imports-schemas all three pin exchangedDocument.notificationStatusCode to {"const": "SUBMITTED"} (checked submitted-v1 line 26), and that repo has no commits on the branch. The dynamics gateway's PimsGbnAgDataMapper and PimsGbnAgDataMapperV2 pass the string through unchanged. Sam's ruling claim 42 lists only the animals frontend, the INS frontend and the stub. His earlier ruling (point 8, 2026-10-09) says no PIMS profile or schema change is made in this programme. So the new value contradicts the declared contract and the stated scope. NotificationIT:938 pins the non-conforming value as correct. Whether PIMS actually rejects the event is unproven, but sending it breaches the declared contract, so high stands.

survived.title: Cancel-amend restores a stale outstanding-items status while document changes made during the amendment stay
survived.what: cancelAmendNotification sets the status from the outstandingItems kept from the last submission. Accompanying documents live in their own collection: an upload made during the amendment is not rolled back on cancel, and a deletion (DocumentService.deleteByUploadId, a hard delete) is not restored. Only notification content and fulfilments are restored. The restored status can therefore contradict the documents the notification holds, and the documents the AmendmentCancelled event lists in referenceDocument (OutboxService reads the live COMPLETE documents). The designed path for clearing 'action required' is Continue, which starts an amendment (inc-113, c-144), so traders will take this path.
survived.scenario: Case A. A notification is SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED. The trader clicks Continue (amend), uploads an ITAHC that scans COMPLETE, then clicks Cancel amend. The status reverts to SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED and the dashboard warns that the certificate is missing, while the event's referenceDocument lists the clean ITAHC. Case B. A notification is SUBMITTED with an ITAHC. The trader amends, deletes the ITAHC, then cancels. The status becomes SUBMITTED with outstandingItems [], but no health certificate exists, and PIMS receives SUBMITTED with no ITAHC reference.
survived.fix: Recompute on cancel as submit does: OutstandingItem.outstandingFor(documentService.findByNotificationRef(referenceNumber)), then set both outstandingItems and the status from that result. Alternatively, snapshot the accompanying-document set at amend and restore it on cancel. Add an IT for the amend, upload ITAHC, cancel-amend path.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed. cancelAmendNotification (line 288) takes the status from the outstandingItems stored at the last submit and never re-reads the documents. Nothing under accompanyingdocument/ mentions amend or cancel, and uploads and deletes have no notification-status guard. So documents added or removed during an amendment survive a cancel, while the status reverts. Meanwhile OutboxService:91 lists the live COMPLETE documents in the event. Case A is the realistic one: the designed recovery is amend, upload the ITAHC, then submit, and a trader who uploads and then cancels stays at action-required with a clean ITAHC on file. The documents not rolling back is older behaviour. The stale status that contradicts them is new in this diff. Medium is right.

survived.title: No IT covers the path that clears action-required, or a clean submit's event
survived.what: The existing outbox event ITs (around lines 1340, 1444 and 1488) were re-pointed from SUBMITTED to SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED instead of being given a clean ITAHC, and their comments still say 'through SUBMITTED'. As a result, no integration test asserts the normal event a correct submit produces: a clean ITAHC giving notificationStatusCode SUBMITTED. No IT drives the designed recovery path either: SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED, then amend, upload a clean ITAHC, resubmit, then SUBMITTED with outstandingItems [] on the stored aggregate and the NotificationSubmissionAmended event. That path is unit-tested only, with DocumentService mocked.
survived.scenario: Suppose a regression makes resubmission ignore documents uploaded during an amendment, for example by reading documents for the wrong reference or reading before the upload is persisted. Every IT stays green, and traders are left stuck at 'Submitted action required' after uploading their certificate.
survived.fix: Add ITs through the real endpoints for both paths. First: submit, amend, givenACleanItahc, submit; assert status SUBMITTED, outstandingItems empty, and the last event's notificationStatusCode. Second: a clean-ITAHC first submit asserting the event's notificationStatusCode is SUBMITTED. Fix the stale 'through SUBMITTED' comments in the re-pointed tests.
survived.verifierNote: Partly overstated but real. A clean-ITAHC submit IT exists (NotificationIT:867), but it asserts only the aggregate status and outstandingItems. It does not check the outbox event's notificationStatusCode, and the only IT on that field is line 938, which pins SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED. No IT drives the path SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED, then amend, upload a clean ITAHC, resubmit. createAndSubmitNotificationWithFullContent seeds the ITAHC before the first submit. The stale comment at line 1341 ('through SUBMITTED') sits above an assertion of SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED, as the reviewer said. This is a test gap only, so low.

results.title: Stub and reference-data
results.summary: I reviewed both changes against origin/main: the stub (inc-173: controllers now serve captured MDM JSON as-is, the six DTOs are deleted, new fixtures and tests) and reference-data (inc-007: PortType, PortListOrder, the traffic mapping and its tests). I checked the fixtures with jq against the raw CDP-test captures and against every consumer. The code is sound. The fixtures match the captures: 250 countries, 32 in the GBNAG_SPS_EX block, 78 ports whose traffic is all Airport, Port or Rail, as in the raw capture. reference-data's model still reads the new shape, and nothing else reads the stub's old fields. What remains is one fixture-provenance gap and three smaller risks, none of them a runtime defect today.
results.answers:
Does the stub still mirror real MDM's contract? Mostly yes, and better than before. Both endpoints now pass through MDM's real record shape: countryUUID, ISONumeric, alpha2{value}, traffic, status and the other fields that used to be dropped. The fixtures are in MDM's order. Unfiltered returns 250 countries and GBNAG_SPS_EX returns 32, which matches raw/getCountries-SPS.json, GB with includeCountry=false included. reference-data's MdmCountry and MdmSubDivision still read the new shape: Boot's default ObjectMapper ignores unknown fields, and subdivision id is an object but reference-data does not model it. Every record except GB keeps effectiveAlias, and reference-data drops GB, so its name sort cannot hit a null. The error contract has not changed: a missing subscription key gives 400 and the key's value is not checked. Real APIM would answer 401, but that existed before this branch. The blocks semantics, and GB's block name, rest on one capture (f2). Only GBNAG_SPS_EX is ever requested by consumers (grep of every repo).

Is reference-data's port typing right for real MDM data? Yes for every value seen: Airport 18, Port 59, Rail 1, the same as the raw capture. traffic is never masked or missing. Mixed or unknown values are kept, typed null and sorted last, as the plan intends, but with no trimming and no signal (f3). The frontends do not read type in production code, so null does not break rendering. No backend consumes /ports-of-entry. The Caffeine cache is in memory, so a deploy is not affected by stale serialised entries.

Fixture provenance: the fixtures come from CDP-test MDM captures taken on 9 October (raw/ is tracked). Masked values were dropped, and effectiveAlias, port names and three townCity values were recovered from tracked reference-data captures. All 78 ports are status active. The regeneration programs and the stub doc are untracked or uncommitted (f1).

Tests: the stub's WebMvcTest tests go through the real HTTP layer and are sound. The reference-data unit test breaks the house mocking rules, and the IT does not cover the edge cases (f4). Out of scope, noted only: stub-ceilings.js now times a 256 KB unfiltered countries body against a stub that used to return 31 slim records, so stub-ceiling perf results from before this branch cannot be compared with results after it.
results.answersCheck: I agree with all three answers. The blocks filter keeps any record that carries a block named GBNAG_SPS_EX (32 records, GB included, matching the spec). The spec does admit the alternative GB-NIR explanation the reviewer flags in f2, so the 'Mostly yes' on contract fidelity is fair, provided the Javadoc and the 'High fidelity' doc row are toned down. On port typing: fromTraffic does no trimming and gives no signal on a miss, as the reviewer says, and an unknown value becomes null and sorts last (the test confirms it). On provenance: confirmed that regenerate/ is untracked and the stub doc is uncommitted. I have one small disagreement. f1 is commit hygiene for the workspace handover with no effect on the shipped code, so it rates low rather than medium. Otherwise I found nothing more in this area. The stub and reference-data changes are sound.

survived.title: The jq programs that rebuild the stub fixtures, and the stub doc, are not committed
survived.what: The 256 KB countries fixture and the ports fixture can only be rebuilt from the raw masked captures by workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/mdm/regenerate/{countries,ports}.jq. `git status` shows that folder as untracked (??). The docs/repos/trade-imports-stub.md edit that names those programs and raises the stub's fidelity from 'Shape only' to 'High' is uncommitted (' M'). The plan said 'the orchestrator commits the workspace', but nothing was committed. The stub repo's own README and the commit say nothing about where the fixtures came from.
survived.scenario: Someone resets or cleans the workspace checkout, or reviews only the stub PR. The jq programs are lost, and with them the only record of which masked fields were left out and which were recovered from cdp-test captures (effectiveAlias, the GBNAG_SPS_EX block names, GB MID's spaces, the townCity values). MDM changes, and nobody can regenerate the fixture the same way. The next person hand-edits 10k lines or recaptures without the masking rules.
survived.fix: Commit regenerate/*.jq and the stub doc edit on the workspace branch of the same name. Add one line to the stub README (or to the commit history the PR carries) pointing to the captures and the regenerate programs.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed: `git status` shows workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/mdm/regenerate/ as untracked and docs/repos/trade-imports-stub.md as modified but not staged. Nothing breaks at runtime. The fixtures are committed in the stub repo and the raw captures are tracked, so regenerating them would be harder but still possible. This is a handover task (commit the programs and the doc on the workspace branch), not a code defect, so I have lowered it to low.

survived.title: The stub's blocks filter is presented as MDM's behaviour, but the evidence also fits another explanation
survived.what: The Javadoc says blocks 'keeps the records that carry that block whatever includeCountry says, as MDM does', and carriesBlock looks only at the country-level blocks[].name. The accepted spec (stub-tidy-up-spec.md:48-49) admits a second explanation: GB may come back because of its GB-NIR subdivision bloc. GB's own 'GBNAG_SPS_EX' block name is also an inference: the jq program renamed every masked '******_EX' token. 35 other block entries have no name at all (masked), so filtering on any block other than GBNAG_SPS_EX returns []. Matching is exact and case-sensitive. Real MDM's behaviour for an unknown block, a comma-separated list or different case is unknown, but [] for an unknown block is now pinned by a test.
survived.scenario: A future consumer asks for blocks=EU, or for a block that a country reaches only through a subdivision bloc. The stub returns [] or a different set from real MDM, and local and CDP-dev tests pass against behaviour that production will not show. Nothing breaks today: reference-data is the only caller, it keeps only includeCountry=true and it drops GB.
survived.fix: Change the Javadoc and the 'High fidelity' doc row to say what was observed (one SPS capture) and that unnamed blocks are not filterable. Confirm the selection rule with the MDM team, or with one more capture of a block reached only through a subdivision, before relying on it.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed. The CountriesController Javadoc (lines 28-31) says 'as MDM does'. stub-tidy-up-spec.md:48-49 itself gives a second explanation (GB could come back through its GB-NIR bloc), and line 79 says the masked block names were left out and GBNAG_SPS_EX was used for the proven entries. carriesBlock is an exact, case-sensitive match on the country-level blocks[].name only. Nothing breaks today: the only caller is reference-data, and it asks for GBNAG_SPS_EX alone (the fixture has 32 matches). The risk is the Javadoc and the fidelity row overclaiming, so low is right.

survived.title: An unrecognised MDM traffic value silently becomes type null and sorts last
survived.what: fromTraffic matches 'Airport', 'Port' and 'Rail' exactly, ignoring case only. It does not trim, and no log or metric records a miss. PortOfEntry maps a miss to null, and PortListOrder puts null types after rail. Every observed value is one of the three, but only CDP-test MDM was captured, not production, and MDM's data is known to be messy (duplicates, 'Teestort', non-breaking spaces).
survived.scenario: Production MDM returns traffic 'Port ' (trailing space), 'Seaport', 'Sea Port' or 'Airport/Port' for a real port. reference-data serves it with "type":null after Folkestone, below every rail port. A user scanning the seaports A to Z does not find it, and nothing in the logs shows that MDM's vocabulary has changed.
survived.fix: Strip the traffic value before matching. Log a warning once per unrecognised value (code plus raw traffic) when a PortOfEntry is built, so production drift shows up. Optionally capture production or pre-production MDM traffic values before release.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed in PortType.fromTraffic (lines 41-48). It uses equalsIgnoreCase with no strip() and logs nothing on a miss. The test keepsAPortOfUnknownTypeLast pins a null type that sorts last. Every captured value matches one of the three, so the trailing-space or 'Seaport' scenario is hypothetical drift in production MDM, not a current fault. Low, and the fix is cheap (strip the value and log a warning on a miss).

survived.title: New reference-data controller test injects mocks into the controller and mocks an internal service
survived.what: The test uses @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension) with @InjectMocks on the controller and mocks MdmService, an in-process collaborator, not the HTTP boundary. docs/best-practices/java/testing/unit.md says never to use @InjectMocks and to test controllers with @WebMvcTest, and Sam's rule is to mock only at the network boundary. The edge cases (null or unknown traffic giving "type":null on the wire, non-breaking spaces, ties broken by code, case-insensitive matching) are proved only on Java objects, never through Feign decoding and Jackson serialisation. The WireMock IT covers six well-formed ports.
survived.scenario: Someone later adds @JsonInclude(NON_NULL), or changes PortType's @JsonValue or deserialisation. Unknown-type ports then lose their type key, or the frontend gets a different wire shape. Every unit test stays green because none of them serialises, and the IT has no unknown-traffic or missing-traffic port to catch it.
survived.fix: Add a port with unknown traffic, one with no traffic and one with a non-breaking space to src/test/resources/integration/mdm-poe-response.json, and assert the order and the "type":null wire shape in PortsOfEntryControllerIT. Test PortListOrder and PortType directly as pure units, with no mocks, and drop the @InjectMocks controller test.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed. PortsOfEntryControllerTest uses @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension), @Mock MdmService and @InjectMocks on the controller. docs/best-practices/java/testing/unit.md:42 says 'Never use @InjectMocks', and the test mocks an in-process service, not the network boundary. Every edge case (unknown or null traffic, NBSP, tie on code, case) is asserted only on Java objects. None of them goes through Feign decoding or the JSON wire shape ("type":null). The breakage scenario is a later regression slipping through, not a present bug, so low.

results.title: Tests repo
results.summary: I reviewed every change in trade-imports-ins-tests from origin/main...HEAD (124 files, 61 commits), comparing the assertions in each changed spec against main, plus the page objects, flows, seeding helpers and commit 65b6afc. Most spec changes follow the Design Release 2.1 rulings, and many assertions are stricter than before: exact toHaveText where main used toContainText, full innerText address checks, and new states for Amend, Submitted and Submitted action required. None of the changes made to beat a flake (the test.slow() calls, the seeded pagination spec, the reordered beforeEach in the read-only address-book specs) dropped or weakened an assertion. The real risks are elsewhere: date checks that now accept the wrong calendar day, an INS dashboard test that locks in a raw status enum shown to users, one assertion that can never fail, a page-object heading that now matches several pages, and reference-list predicates left loose after the themes were merged. Commit 65b6afc is superseded and not needed.
results.answers:
(a) Every test.slow() added: commit 26273b2 adds it to commercial-transporter-scope and private-transporter-scope. Commit 7f9cbfa adds it to promoted-lifecycle (amend re-entry), api-seed-parity and both persistence-notification tests. Brand-new specs carry their own: opening-run x5, overview-task-return x2, horse-temporary-admission, amend-review-heading (the document test), additional-details-scope (the new test), hub-groups-and-cya-rows (the overland test) and promoted-documents (the document-card test). Comparing each against main, every one is a one-line addition with no step or assertion removed. The commit messages blame longer journeys: each task now saves back to the Overview, which adds two page loads per task. That fits the diff (journey.ts adds overview.heading.waitFor and a task click after each section). None of them weakens an assertion.

(b) Dashboard pagination (5c0da51): main clicked 'Start a new notification' 26 times. The branch POSTs to the same create route 26 times through FrontendFormClient (createEmptyNotification), then opens the dashboard. Every assertion is unchanged: the 'Showing 1 to 25 of N', next and previous links, the page=2 URL and a different first card. This is seeding as set-up for a one-page assertion, which the rule allows. The button's own behaviour is still covered by reference-strip, auth, notification-dashboard.spec:35 and the startNotification flow. Not weakened. One pre-existing caveat: the `\d+` total means the test relies on the seed context and the browser being the same stub user.

(c) The read-only address-book beforeEach change (addresses-read-only.spec.ts): the shared beforeEach walked a whole notification and then skipped one test of each pair. Each test now calls skip first and only then walks via openPartyPicker. The steps and all four assertions per test are identical to main. Not weakened; it only saves the walk in a test that is going to be skipped.

(d) Other changes made to beat a flake: (1) commit 3e7b227 widened the plants confirmation date to yesterday, today or tomorrow, and the same tolerance appears in the new animals and plants date-submitted and date-created checks. That is a real weakening (finding f1). (2) f510245, 1250a12, e69bb75 and 87477c3 loosened the reference-list post-save checks to 'any page other than import reason'. They were transitional and are still loose after the merge (finding f5). (3) promoted-lifecycle, aggregated-notification, the outbox specs, notification-submission and frontend-lifecycle moved from SUBMITTED to SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED. That follows the new status, not a flake. They now use exact toHaveText or toBe, which is stricter than main's toContainText('Submitted'). The dropped assertions on main (journeyStrip 'Amending'/'Submitted', the 'Import details' and 'Cow (0102) — Bos taurus' cards, the phone and email rows, 'Not provided' x4 becoming x2, the transit page's empty-list sentence) are all replaced by equivalent or stricter checks that match the Design Release 2.1 copy. Contact and party cards now assert that phone and email are absent, per the design.

(e) Seeded journeys: flows/animals/seeded-journey.ts gains createSubmittedNotificationWithHealthCertificate and createSubmittedNotificationWithDocument (a multipart upload through the frontend, polling scan status), and createSubmittedNotification now yields Submitted action required. domain/animals/fixtures/seeded-journey.ts gains the ITAHC and commercial-invoice document fields. Every caller uses them as set-up for a one-page assertion: confirmation.spec, notification-view-states, notification-dashboard, amend-review-heading, amend-endings, soft-save, stale-arrival-date and the no-JS cancel-amend test. No journey spec is seeded. The journey proofs (opening-run, horse-temporary-admission, overview-task-return, hub-groups) walk the UI. notificationApi.overwriteStoredAnswer (stale-arrival-date) writes the fulfilments directly. That is the only way to make a saved date go stale and is set-up for one page, so it is acceptable, but it leaves the notification's shape fields empty until the next save, as its own doc comment says. Callers that relied on the old 'Submitted' result were updated to use the WithHealthCertificate variant, and no loose toContainText('Submitted') checks remain in tests/animals or tests/ins.

(f) Page objects that hide real behaviour: notificationView.heading (animals and plants) now matches any review or view H1 (finding f4). AnimalsArrivalDetailsPage.selectPort falls back to selectOption when the field is still a native SELECT, which would hide a broken type-ahead with JS on. port-of-entry-select.spec drives and checks the combobox directly, though, and plants already had this pattern on main, so the risk is low and not raised. clearChoices and removeRegionCodeMaxLength change the DOM on purpose to send a crafted request to the server. They are named for that and used only in soft-save, so they are fine. statusTag is `main .govuk-tag`; if a page ever shows two tags this fails loudly in strict mode rather than hiding anything.

(g) 65b6afc: it is only on backup/inc-107-leaked-commit; no other branch contains it, and none of its content is on the combined branch. It is superseded by 02dd6bc, which landed the same document-card test with alphanumeric references and an existing JPG fixture. The PNG fixture, the .gitignore negation and the PW-TXT rename are not needed. Verdict: delete the branch (finding f6). Side note outside the tests repo: the backend rejects non-alphanumeric document references (`@Pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9]*$`), but the animals frontend has no matching format rule. A trader typing 'UK-123' would get a backend 400 rather than a page error. That is probably what led the build to switch to alphanumeric references, and it deserves its own look in the frontend area.
results.answersCheck: I agree with answers (a), (b), (c), (e) and (g). (d)(1) is right that the date tolerance is a real weakening, but it understates the cause: plants-frontend already runs with TZ=Europe/London (Dockerfile), and the backend's zone-less LocalDateTime is parsed as London time. So the confirmation, 'Date submitted' and 'Date created' pages show the UTC calendar day between 00:00 and 01:00 BST. That is a live product bug the widened tests hide, not a hypothetical one. The same zone-less pattern probably applies wherever these dates are formatted. (f): I disagree that notificationView.heading hides real behaviour in the cited spec, because addresses-submit-freeze follows each heading check with a statusTag assertion. The H1 widening follows the design, where a draft's review and a submitted view share the reference heading. The f2 point about the INS raw enum is a pre-existing, ruled interim state (INS dashboard rows are blocked pending re-distil per ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm section (j)), not a defect this diff introduced. The side note in (g) about the backend's alphanumeric @Pattern on documentReference, which the frontend does not match, is still worth checking in the frontend area. I did not verify it beyond confirming that the frontend's file-type check runs first.

survived.title: Date checks accept yesterday at any hour, hiding an off-by-one-day bug
survived.what: Commit 3e7b227 widened the plants confirmation 'Date of notification' check to accept yesterday, today or tomorrow. The animals view's 'Date created' and 'Date submitted' checks (notification-view-states.spec.ts:40, 183, 266) and the plants ones (review.spec.ts:412, 629) accept yesterday or today. The commit says the extra day is only needed in the hour after midnight BST, but the tests accept it at every hour of the day. The plants backend stores submittedAt as a LocalDateTime with no zone (NotificationAggregate.java:50), and the confirmation controller reads it with new Date(value) before formatting for Europe/London. The date shown is therefore only right when the frontend process runs in UTC, and the tests cannot catch it being wrong.
survived.scenario: The plants frontend runs with TZ=Europe/London (native dev, or a container setting changes). At 14:00 a trader submits on 12 October. The zone-less submittedAt is read as London time, so a UTC-to-London regression can push the date a day off. If the page shows 11 October, review.spec.ts:201 and :412 still pass because yesterday is in the accepted set. The same applies to the animals 'Date submitted' header.
survived.fix: Accept the previous day only when the London clock is between 00:00 and 01:00 (compute the expected set from the current time), or read submittedAt back through the API and format it in Europe/London to get one expected string. results.title: Performance tests
results.summary: I reviewed the whole trade-imports-performance-tests diff (origin/main...HEAD, 3 commits, 7 files) against the live-animals frontend's new RUN_STEPS and flow.js on the combined branch. The import-reason move is correct: the first six k6 steps now match Design Release 2.1. After additional-details, though, the k6 walk still does not follow the real opening run, and the change missed the frontend dropping cph-number from the run. Neither shows up in any check, because walker.reach quietly opens a page directly when the previous save landed somewhere else. No threshold or measurement was weakened. The new missed-page logging is useful but only covers the INS dashboard, and it logs on every iteration, including the OIDC callback URL.
results.answers:
1. Does the k6 journey still match the real order after the opening-run change? Only partly. The first six steps (origin, commodities, import-reason, consignment-details, identification, additional-details) now match RUN_STEPS in animals-frontend flow/run.js. After that the k6 walk goes documents, addresses, cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, contact. The real run goes port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, documents, addresses, contact. Part of that gap was there on main. The opening-run change made it one step worse: it removed cph-number from RUN_STEPS (it is now reached only from the addresses page) and the k6 still treats it as a run step. It also added endsRunWhenComplete on addresses, so a complete notification lands on the hub. See perf-f1.

The identification step is also always reached, even when no commodity needs identifiers and the real run skips it. That predates this change and is untouched.

The import-reason answers still work with the changed page: internalMarket plus breeding, with no country or port field needed. That page's country list moved to destinationCountryOptions, which these answers do not use.

2. Do checks fail loudly on a missed page? Only on the INS dashboard. There, 'INS dashboard opens signed in' still feeds the checks threshold, and a miss now logs what the page showed instead. Journey steps do not. walker.reach silently opens the expected page when a save landed elsewhere, and saved() passes any 200 save that was not stale and did not loop on redirects, even if it landed on the hub or the wrong page. A non-200 save does fail its check and ends the iteration (runSteps returns ok:false). So a page that errors fails loudly, but a page reached out of order does not. describeMissedPage is not wired into reach or saved.

3. Was any threshold or measurement weakened? No. The diff does not touch thresholds.js, traffic.js, pages.js or journeys.js. The dashboard check's predicate is the same: status 200 and heading 'Dashboard', the latter still read from the first h1. The INS frontend's change on this branch only alters the <title> format, not the h1. The only side effect on measurement is indirect: the extra direct GETs from perf-f1 eat into the pages-per-notification budget that reEditUntilTarget pads.
results.answersCheck: I agree with all three answers. On Q1, I verified that RUN_STEPS on the branch is origin, commodities, import-reason, consignment-details, identification, additional-details, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, documents, addresses (endsRunWhenComplete), contact, notification-view. I also verified that the frontend diff is what removed cph-number. One nuance the reviewer stated but underweighted: most of the tail mismatch predates this branch. The only new drift is the addresses → cph-number transition, so I rate the impact low, not medium. When k6 reaches addresses, contact is not yet saved, so readyForCheckYourAnswers is false and the addresses save lands on contact, not the hub. The hub ending does not happen in the k6 walk. On Q2, I confirmed that reach falls back silently (pages.js:150-153) and that saved() only runs a check on isSaved. On Q3, I confirmed the diff touches only journey-endpoints key order, the draft order, front-door logging, and the new missed-page lib and tests. No thresholds, traffic or pages.js changes.

survived.what: The frontend's RUN_STEPS (animals-frontend src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js) now runs origin, commodities, import-reason, consignment-details, identification, additional-details, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, documents, addresses (endsRunWhenComplete), contact, notification-view. Model cph-number as a detour inside the addresses step: open it from the addresses page, save it, land back on addresses, then save addresses. Drop it from its own top-level slot. Change live-animals.test.js to assert the full draft order. The k6 draft in src/k6/live-animals.js (lines 208-218) still walks documents, addresses, cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, contact. walker.reach in src/k6/pages.js:150 keeps the landed page only when the status is 200 and the path matches. The only new drift is addresses → cph-number: main's run went from addresses to cph-number, and now it goes to contact. That is about one extra direct GET per notification. results.title: Workspace tooling
results.summary: I reviewed the workspace tooling diff (3c28ff5a~1..HEAD) across tim exec (stack, stack-lease, stack-refresh, stack-fingerprints, docker-daemon), tim build gate, tim backlog split, split-off and themes, tim distil, and the increment-build-loop workflow. The backlog split-off, relink, distil and x-refresh-with code is sound and well tested. The main defect: when Docker Desktop has quit, tim now starts it again inside every `docker ps`, and the gate then treats the run's own down stack as one it started itself. It releases that stack after the e2e rungs, which takes it down and deletes the run's lease. So the new recover-and-re-lease path almost never runs. A second risk: the new rollback step in the failed-attempt handler soft-resets every unpushed commit in each repo, not just the failed attempt's. Neither lets wrong code land green; both affect lease safety and keeping the branch's history intact.
results.answersCheck: The reviewer answered no explicit questions. The summary's claims hold: I traced the f1 lease teardown end to end through gate.js, stack-lease.js and stack.js and confirmed the soft-reset scope in f2. I disagree with f2's severity. The scenario needs a push-failed stop, a relaunch before the human reconciles the branch, and a different row's red ladder before A is pushed, and the commits survive as patch files, so I rate it low, not medium. For f3, I also disagree in part: stopping on gaps that predate the theme within prefixes it touched looks like intended policy. Only the over-inclusion of prefixes through 'repo reach' is a clear defect.

survived.title: Gate tears down and deletes the run's own lease after Docker Desktop quits
survived.what: psStackWithDocker (tim/src/exec/stack.js:159) now starts Docker Desktop again whenever docker ps says the daemon is unreachable. In the gate, takeLease calls acquireStack as RUN_HOLDER. The run's lease is state UP, and Docker came back with no containers (the stack sets no restart policies). So acquireDecision returns 'start', startUnderLease rebuilds the stack, and lease.started is true. runE2e's finally block then calls giveBack, and releaseStack runs stop-stack.sh and removes the lease file. The gate cannot tell 'I started a free stack' apart from 'I restarted my own run's stack'. Before this change, an unreachable daemon made takeLease fail. The stage reported it, and the new recoverDownStack in the loop would have taken the lease again.
survived.scenario: An overnight branch run holds the lease as ibl-…, and a Homebrew cask upgrade quits Docker Desktop. The ladder's `tim build gate --phase e2e --holder ibl-…` starts Docker, rebuilds the stack, runs the e2e rungs green, then stops the stack and deletes the lease. The next stage runs `tim docker lease status`: lease null, up false. By RUN_STACK_RULE that means stackHeld with holder null, and confirmStackHeld believes it (null !== RUN_HOLDER). The run stops as 'stack-held' and preserves the attempt; or, where no stage checks, every later e2e gate cold-starts the stack and tears it down. Between gates the stack has no lease, so another session can take it. The end-of-run release finds nothing to release. The stackDown → recoverDownStack path only fires when a stage reads the lease before any gate has 'healed' it.
survived.fix: Make acquireStack return whether the start replaced the holder's own lease (previous?.holder === holder), and have runE2e give the stack back only when the gate took a lease nobody held before (lease.started && !lease.resumedOwnLease). Add a gate test: own UP lease, Docker quit, e2e runs, then assert the lease is still the holder's and the stack is up.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed on the branch. The ladder's e2e gate runs with --holder RUN_HOLDER (increment-build-loop.js:945). takeLease (gate.js:259) calls acquireStack, and stackStatus now goes through psStackWithDocker (stack.js:159), which reopens Docker Desktop instead of throwing. The compose files under docker/stack set no `restart:` policy, so the stack comes back with no containers. acquireDecision (stack-lease.js:146) then returns 'start' for the holder's own UP lease when up is false. startUnderLease returns started:true, gate.js:429 calls giveBack, and releaseStack runs stop-stack.sh and removes the lease file. stack-lease.js and gate.js's lease logic are unchanged in the diff. Before the diff, though, the daemon-down case threw inside takeLease ('Can't tell whether the workspace stack is free') and never reached this path, so the diff is what makes it reachable. Unit and FIT gate phases' port checks now reopen Docker too, so the ladder's e2e gate is usually the first thing to see the down stack. recoverDownStack only runs if a stage reads the lease first. After that, a stage sees lease null and stops as stack-held (confirmStackHeld treats a null holder as not this run's), or every later e2e gate cold-starts and releases the stack. Medium is right: it costs lease safety and run continuity, but no wrong code lands green. Suggested fix: carry 'restarted own lease' from acquireStack and skip giveBack in that case.

survived.title: Failed-attempt handler's soft reset sweeps up commits that are not the attempt's
survived.what: New step 0 of the branch-lifecycle preserve prompt treats every commit in `origin/<branch>..HEAD` as the failed attempt's work. It writes them out as a patch, then runs `reset --soft origin/<branch>`, and later steps stash the result. That rests on 'No stage commits: only landing does, and it pushes at once'. But the loop has a push-failed outcome that leaves a landed, recorded, unpushed commit on the branch by design ('a resume pushes the recorded commit'). The branch baseline (branchBaselinePrompt) never checks the ahead count, and a person's own unpushed commit on the theme branch also passes the clean-tree baseline.
survived.scenario: Row A lands, its push is rejected because the remote moved, and the run stops push-failed with A's commit SHA recorded. The person relaunches with an explicit id queue, or the derived order puts row B first. B's ladder goes red, and preserveAttempt soft-resets A's commit together with B's work into B's failure stash. A's row still records its commit, so A resumes past build. The find-PRs stage sees nothing ahead to push and marks A done. A's change never reaches the branch, and survives only in logs/<B>-preserve-*.commits.patch.
survived.fix: Either make the baseline refuse to start a row when any configured repo has commits ahead of origin/<branch> (or push them first, as the find-PRs stage does), or have step 0 reset only commits made after a HEAD SHA the loop records at the start of the row's baseline.
survived.verifierNote: Step 0 (increment-build-loop.js:1510-1517, added in 4d734946) does soft-reset everything in origin/<branch>..HEAD in every configured repo. The push-failed outcome (4363-4371) does leave a recorded, unpushed commit, and branchBaselinePrompt (2848) checks only the branch and clean trees, never the ahead count. So the scenario can happen. It needs three things: a push-failed stop, a relaunch before the human reconciles the branch (which the code comment expects them to do), and a different row's red ladder before A is pushed. A different row comes first only with an explicit id queue or a derived order that puts B first. Nothing is lost outright: the commits go to logs/<B>-preserve-*.commits.patch and the note names their SHAs. A's row would still show a commit that is not on the branch, though, which is a silent integrity gap. The scenario is narrow and the work can be recovered, so low rather than medium. The fix the reviewer suggests (refuse at baseline when ahead > 0, or record a per-row HEAD and reset only past it) is sound.

survived.title: Theme spec check stops the run on gaps that predate the theme, and on prefixes the theme never touched
survived.what: themeSpecCheck turns any `tim spec gaps --none` noneCount > 0, or any lint finding, across the whole prefix into a 'spec-check-red' stop. That includes gaps that predate the theme. It also adds every prefix reachable from the repos of theme rows this run did not build. A row with no `repos` counts as touching every configured repo, and animals-backend maps to both live-animals and germinal-products.
survived.scenario: A theme was built over two launches, and its earlier rows changed only trade-imports-animals-backend for live animals. When the last row lands, the 'repo reach' source adds germinal-products/. That prefix has unproven scenarios from before this programme, so the run stops with SPEC CHECK RED and prescribes 'catch-up and cover germinal' for a set the theme never touched.
survived.fix: Compare against a per-prefix gaps baseline taken at the run's (or theme's) first baseline and stop only on new noneScenarios. For rows not built in this run, use the prefixes recorded in their landed Spec sync lines, which are already parsed, instead of repo reach.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed. prefixesBySource (3243-3250) adds 'repo reach' for rows this run did not build. SPEC_PREFIXES_BY_REPO_PATH (753-762) maps both animals repos to ['live-animals','germinal-products']. gapsProblem (3209) turns any noneCount > 0 into a problem, and themeSpecCheck stops the run with spec-check-red. A theme built over two launches can therefore stop on germinal-products gaps it never touched, and the run prescribes 'catch-up and cover germinal'. Stopping on gaps that predate the theme within prefixes the theme did touch is arguably the intended strict policy, given Sam's 'failures are mine to fix' stance. The repo-reach over-inclusion is the real defect. The effect is a false stop at the end of a theme with a clear message, not wrong code, so low. survived.title: Read-only stack queries now launch Docker Desktop and can block for 5 minutes

results.title: Backend fetch timeout and retry
results.summary: I reviewed backend-fetch.js and its tests, the vitest set-up shim and the errors.js cause logging. The animals and plants frontends carry the same file (blob d1664a3 in both). I also reviewed the animals FIT timeout raise and checked both against the build's stack logs and the GitHub Actions runs. On CDP the change does nothing useful, because HTTP_PROXY is set there, so the 2s bound never applies and the retry almost never fires. It also splits backend calls into two fetch/FormData paths, and no test environment now runs the CDP one. It was tested through a library mock that hides what it sends. My verdict is to remove it from production code, keeping stackWithCauses. The FIT timeout raise covers real set-up cost, not flakes (0 retries).
results.answers:
(1) Is it needed in CDP? No. All the evidence is local. Every ConnectTimeoutError in the build's logs (workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/themes/overview-and-review/logs/*/gate-stack-after-...-frontend-1.log) is to 192.168.65.254 / fdc4:f303:9324::254, Docker Desktop's host-gateway address for host.docker.internal: port 8085 (animals backend), 8091 (plants backend) and also 8089 (address book, which backendFetch does not cover, so even locally the fix is partial). There is no CDP evidence. In CDP the calls go service to service through the platform proxy, not through Docker Desktop's forwarder. No log exists from after the fix either: there is no 'timeout: 2000ms' or UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT anywhere in the workarea, and the last rerun log (20:13Z) predates 19a76c54 (20:26Z), so whether it fixed anything locally is also unproven.

(2) Does it behave behind CDP's HTTP_PROXY? It does not bypass the proxy. When config httpProxy (HTTP_PROXY) is set, `dispatcher` is undefined, so calls use the built-in fetch and the global ProxyAgent from setup-proxy.js (setGlobalDispatcher; undici 8 also publishes a wrapped copy under the legacy 'undici.globalDispatcher.1' symbol that Node 24's fetch reads). Backend calls therefore go through the proxy exactly as they did before this change. Whether they should is a separate, pre-existing question. undici's ProxyAgent ignores NO_PROXY (only EnvHttpProxyAgent honours it), and config reads only HTTP_PROXY, so every undici and built-in fetch call, internal ones included, goes to squid. The flip side is that in CDP the 2s bound never applies: the default 10s connect timeout to the proxy stays. The retry fires only if the socket to squid itself fails. A backend squid cannot reach comes back as a 5xx response, or as RequestAbortedError 'Proxy response (503) !== 200 when HTTP Tunneling' for https, and neither is retried. So in CDP the change is effectively dead code, and it leaves CDP on a different fetch/FormData path from every test environment (f1).

(3) Is a retry safe for non-idempotent calls? Mostly. UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT (which covers the TCP and TLS handshake) and ECONNREFUSED happen before any request bytes are written, so a create, submit or upload cannot be duplicated through them. With a proxy, they only concern the hop to the proxy. ETIMEDOUT is the exception: it can come from an established keep-alive socket after the request was written, so POST submit/create/copy/upload could in principle be sent twice (f3, low; it is unlikely within undici's 300s headersTimeout). The retry also covers every method, with no idempotency guard.

The 2s figure: it does not apply in CDP, so CDP cold starts do not matter for it. A container that is not ready refuses quickly or answers 5xx through the proxy, and connect latency is not the issue. Locally, 2s is reasonable for a stalled forwarder. During a backend restart, the immediate retry on ECONNREFUSED just fails a second time.

Error mapping: unchanged for callers. The final error is the second attempt's TypeError 'fetch failed', which becomes a Boom 500. The new stackWithCauses in errors.js (logging each cause under 'Caused by:') is a real diagnostic improvement and worth keeping on its own.

Multipart and streaming: uploadFile already built an in-memory Blob before this change, so it never streamed. The undici FormData copy references the same File and does not copy bytes. After d66b1dce the multipart filename and part type are intact (proven by the real-connection test). Downloads still stream: the npm undici Response body is a web ReadableStream, and Readable.fromWeb in download.js:11 works (tested).

Verdict: remove from production code in both frontends. Revert backendFetch to plain fetch and delete test/setup-backend-fetch.js, backend-fetch.real.test.js and the retry unit tests. Keep stackWithCauses. Sam's rule allows a client connect-timeout and retry where evidence names the call, and the evidence does name 8085/8091. If he wants that kept, keep but narrow:
- Apply the bound locally only, through one global Agent with a connect timeout set in setup-proxy's no-proxy branch behind a stack-only env flag (built-in fetch already honours an npm undici global dispatcher), so there is no second fetch or FormData.
- Retry only on UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT/ECONNREFUSED, ideally only for idempotent methods.
- Test it against real sockets, not a library mock.

FIT timeout 900s → 1500s: it grew because the suite went from 455 to 529 tests and from 12.7m to 18.0m (CI runs 38217892519 on main and 38219575045 on combined), with 0 flaky and 0 retries. It is not masking flakes. It is absorbing set-up cost: one-page assertions about submitted or amending notifications each drive a full journey in beforeEach (about 16s per test, 20 tests over 15s against 1 on main). Main was already using 85% of the 900s budget. See f4.
results.answersCheck: I agree with answers (1) to (3) in substance. (1): I confirmed that the pre-fix ConnectTimeoutErrors point at 192.168.65.254:8085 with a 10000ms timeout, which is local Docker Desktop host-gateway evidence. I did not re-verify the 8089 address-book or post-fix log-absence claims. (2): setup-proxy.js:17-21 sets a global ProxyAgent only when HTTP_PROXY is set, and backend-fetch.js:22-23 then leaves CDP on built-in fetch through that proxy. So the 2s bound never applies in CDP, and only failures on the socket to the proxy are retried. I agree. (3): I agree that UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT and ECONNREFUSED are pre-send failures and that ETIMEDOUT is the exception. Where I disagree: the reviewer implies retry behaviour is untested ('passes with the feature removed'). backend-fetch.test.js:73-108 does test the retry decision through the shimmed global fetch, so removing the retry branch fails the unit suite. What is truly untested is the 2s bound and the agent. On the FIT timeout, the full-journey beforeEach for 'submitted notification' pre-dates the build on main. The build grew it (more tests, plus the upload step) rather than introducing it. I agree with the verdict to remove the fork and keep stackWithCauses. If a bound is kept, putting it on the global dispatcher behind a stack-only flag is the right shape, given npm undici's legacy-symbol install.

survived.title: Two divergent HTTP paths; the CDP path is no longer exercised by any test environment
survived.what: connectBoundedDispatcher() returns undefined whenever HTTP_PROXY is set, so fetchOnce (line 58) splits behaviour by environment. Unit, FIT and the local E2E stack (no HTTP_PROXY: docker/stack sets none) send through npm undici 8.11.2's fetch, with an undici FormData copy and a private Agent. CDP, which injects HTTP_PROXY, sends through Node's built-in fetch, with Node's FormData, through the global ProxyAgent. The comment at lines 17-20 says the fork is needed because built-in fetch 'rejects' npm undici agents. The pre-fix logs show otherwise. inc-109-ladder-e2e-rerun at 20:13Z, before 19a76c54 at 20:26Z, shows built-in fetch already connecting through /home/node/node_modules/undici/lib/core/connect.js with a 10000ms timeout. This is because npm undici's lib/global.js installs its Agent under both 'undici.globalDispatcher.2' and, wrapped in a Dispatcher1Wrapper, the legacy '.1' symbol. So the parallel fetch was never needed. In CDP the change adds nothing: there is no 2s bound, and the retry fires only if the socket to the squid proxy itself fails. A backend the proxy cannot reach comes back as a 502/503 response (http target) or as RequestAbortedError 'Proxy response (503) !== 200 when HTTP Tunneling' (https target), and neither is in CONNECT_ERROR_CODES.
survived.scenario: A future change to how bodies or headers are built (another FormData field, a stream body, a Blob subclass) passes unit, FIT and local E2E because all of them take the undici path, then breaks only in CDP on the built-in fetch path. The reverse has already happened: 19a76c54 sent every upload as text/plain on the undici path, and the backend refused it with HttpMediaTypeNotSupportedException. d66b1dce had to patch that in, and only the E2E baseline caught it.
survived.fix: Revert backendFetch to `countBackendCall(); return fetch(url, init)`, and drop asUndiciFormData/forUndici and test/setup-backend-fetch.js. If a local connect bound is still wanted, set it in one place without forking fetch: for example, in setup-proxy's no-proxy branch call `setGlobalDispatcher(new Agent({ connect: { timeout } }))` from npm undici, which built-in fetch already honours through the legacy symbol. Gate it behind a stack-only env var, so CDP and the tests run the same fetch and FormData.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed. backend-fetch.js:21-26 returns no dispatcher when httpProxy is set, so fetchOnce (line 58) sends CDP calls through built-in fetch, Node FormData and the global ProxyAgent, while unit, FIT and the local stack go through npm undici fetch, an undici FormData copy and a private Agent. The fork was not needed. npm undici's lib/global.js installs its Agent under 'undici.globalDispatcher.2' and also, wrapped in Dispatcher1Wrapper, under the legacy '.1' symbol. The pre-fix log inc-109-ladder-e2e-rerun (20:13:49Z) shows built-in fetch failing inside /home/node/node_modules/undici/lib/core/connect.js with 'timeout: 10000ms'. So setGlobalDispatcher(new Agent({connect:{timeout}})) in a stack-only branch would have bounded the connect without a second fetch path. The 19a76c54 → d66b1dce text/plain upload regression shows this divergence already broke once. Medium is right: no CDP break today, but nothing exercises the CDP path any more.

survived.title: Unit tests cannot see what is actually sent; the real-connection tests pass with the feature removed
survived.what: A global setupFiles vi.mock('undici') replaces undici.fetch with a shim that strips `dispatcher` and converts undici FormData back to Node FormData before calling the mocked global fetch. That mocks a library and rewrites its arguments, rather than mocking at the network boundary. Every unit test of a backend call therefore sees a request shape production never sends, and the conversion code in backend-fetch.js (forUndici/asUndiciFormData) is not observable to them. In backend-fetch.real.test.js, 'tries a refused connection once more' (line 104) only asserts the final ECONNREFUSED, which it gets with or without a retry. 'reaches the backend through its connect-bounded agent' (line 18) passes with the agent removed. No test exercises the 2s bound.
survived.scenario: Delete the retry branch (lines 74-78) or the `dispatcher` from forUndici: every real-connection test still passes. A FormData conversion bug like the one 19a76c54 shipped passes the whole unit suite, because the shim reconverts the body before any assertion sees it.
survived.fix: If the code is removed (f1), delete the shim and the real test. If any of it is kept, test only against a real local server: count 'connection' events to prove exactly two attempts, and use a listener that accepts the TCP connection but never answers TLS, or MockAgent, to prove the time bound. Do not mock undici globally in setupFiles.
survived.verifierNote: Partly real. The setupFiles vi.mock('undici') in test/setup-backend-fetch.js:9-26 strips the dispatcher and converts undici FormData back to Node FormData. Unit tests therefore cannot see the agent or the FormData conversion, and it mocks a library rather than the network boundary. In the real-connection tests, test 1 passes with no agent and test 4 (line 104) asserts only the final ECONNREFUSED, so neither proves a second attempt. Nothing tests the 2s bound. The scenario overstates one point: deleting the retry branch at lines 74-78 WOULD fail backend-fetch.test.js:73-89, which drives the retry through the shim. The FormData gap is now partly closed by the real multipart test at lines 37-77. What remains is an unproven timeout and agent, plus a library-level mock, so low rather than medium.

survived.title: ETIMEDOUT in the retry set is not guaranteed to mean the request was never sent
survived.what: The retry runs for every method, including POST /notifications (create), /{id}/copy, /{id}/submit, /amend, /soft-delete, /notifications/{id}/document-uploads and /document-uploads/{id}/file. It fires if any cause in the chain has UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, ECONNREFUSED or ETIMEDOUT. The first two can only happen before any request bytes are sent, including during the TLS handshake for an https target, so retrying on them is safe. ETIMEDOUT can also be raised on an established keep-alive socket, from a kernel keepalive or retransmission failure after the request has been written. The logs only show ETIMEDOUT nested under UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT (AggregateError from internalConnectMultiple), so it adds no coverage.
survived.scenario: POST /notifications/{id}/submit is written on a reused keep-alive socket and the backend commits it. The path then drops before the response arrives and the socket errors with ETIMEDOUT. backendFetch sends the submit again, and the second call gets a 409 or state error, or (on create or copy) a duplicate notification. Unlikely within undici's 300s headersTimeout, but possible, and nothing guards against it.
survived.fix: If the retry survives, limit CONNECT_ERROR_CODES to UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT and ECONNREFUSED, and preferably retry only GET/PUT/DELETE, or require an idempotency key for POST.
survived.verifierNote: ETIMEDOUT is in CONNECT_ERROR_CODES at line 14, and isConnectError walks the whole cause chain for every method, including POST submit, create and copy. undici's h1 client passes a socket error on an established socket straight to in-flight requests as the raw error, unless it is ECONNRESET at message end. So a kernel ETIMEDOUT after the request was written would be retried. The unit test at backend-fetch.test.js:110 shows the intent is not to resend once the connection has opened, and ETIMEDOUT contradicts that intent. It is rare and needs a mid-flight path drop. Low.

survived.title: FIT global timeout raised to fit full-journey set-up repeated per one-page test
survived.what: d1884244 raised --global-timeout from 900000 to 1500000, and the FIT job timeout-minutes from 20 to 30 (.github/workflows/check-pull-request.yml:115), because the suite outgrew 900s. survived.title: Transit and destination lists now offer subdivision codes that reach GBN-AG as raw country IDs

In the backend, TradeCountry.fromCountryCodes (outbox/gbnag/TradeCountry.java:21-27) wraps each string as CodedValue.of(code) with a null subdivision, and SpecifiedConsignment.java:43 sends that list. killed.title: The error handler logs a plain string, so the err serialiser never runs
killed.what: catchAll now calls request.logger.error(stackWithCauses(response)) with a plain string. This misses the pino { err } pattern in docs/best-practices/node/pino-logging.md section 11. The err serialiser that produces ECS error.type, error.message and error.stack_trace never runs, so 5xx errors reach CDP's log aggregator as an unstructured message, and alerting or searching on error.* fields finds nothing. pino-std-serializers' err serialiser already folds each cause's stack in, so the hand-rolled helper is not needed. The helper's while (cause) loop also has no guard against a cause chain that loops back on itself, which would hang the onPreResponse handler.
killed.scenario: A backend call fails with TypeError('fetch failed', { cause: ConnectTimeoutError }). The 500 is logged as one string in the message field with no error.type or error.stack_trace, so a CDP dashboard filtering on error.type misses it. Separately, an error whose cause chain loops back to itself (a.cause = b, b.cause = a) makes catchAll loop forever.
killed.fix: Replace the call with request.logger.error({ err: response }, 'Unhandled error response') and delete stackWithCauses and its test. If the cause text is still wanted in the message, rely on the serialiser's cause handling rather than a custom loop.
killed.refutation: The main claim is not a regression from this diff. On main the line was already request.logger.error(response?.stack), which also logs a plain string with no { err } object, so the ECS error.* fields were already missing before the build. The change only adds the cause stacks to a message that was already a string, which is an improvement on main. The infinite-loop part needs a cause chain that loops back on itself. Neither undici's 'fetch failed' wrapping nor Boom produces one, and the reviewer gives no real source. Switching to { err: response } is a fair hardening suggestion, but no failure scenario holds for code this diff introduced.

results.title: Plants frontend shared code

It drops only string.empty, any.required and a blank any.only, so format rules still refuse on hub exit. commodity-type's blank-type path cannot drop lines, because linesDroppedBy returns removed: 0 when there is no type.

- Unit tests: `npm --prefix …/trade-imports-plants-frontend run test` on the touched shared folders: 19 files, 394 tests, all passing.
results.answersCheck: There were no explicit questions. The soft-save scope matches inc-003's AC5. On f2 I disagree with the framing: the difference from animals is not 'plants lacks what animals has'.
