killed.title: stackWithCauses loops forever on a cyclic error cause
killed.what: The new stackWithCauses follows error.cause with `while (cause)` and has no record of causes already seen and no depth cap. It runs in onPreResponse for every 5xx. If an error's cause chain refers back to itself (a.cause = b, b.cause = a, or err.cause = err, which some wrapper libraries and hand-written rethrows produce), the loop never ends. Each pass pushes another stack string, so the event loop blocks and memory grows until the process is OOM-killed. The animals copy is identical.
killed.scenario: A handler throws an Error whose cause chain loops (for example, a retry wrapper sets `lastError.cause = error` after `error.cause = lastError`). Boom turns it into a 500, catchAll calls stackWithCauses, the loop never exits, and that instance stops serving every user until CDP restarts it.
killed.fix: Track seen causes in a Set and stop on a repeat, or cap the depth (for example 10). Apply the same fix in trade-imports-animals-frontend/src/server/common/helpers/errors.js so the two copies stay the same.
killed.refutation: The loop in src/server/common/helpers/errors.js:18-27 does have no cycle guard, but the review gives no way to make it spin. I grepped every place plants src sets a cause: get-oidc-config-with-retry.js:20, services/countries/index.js:27 and services/ports/index.js:26. Each wraps a fresh `new Error(..., { cause: err })` one level deep, and nothing assigns `.cause` back up the chain. undici's 'fetch failed' errors also have acyclic causes. The 'retry wrapper' in the scenario does not exist in this codebase. It is a cheap hardening (keep a Set of seen causes), and backend-fetch.js:30-35 walks causes the same unguarded way, but it is not a defect the diff makes reachable.

killed.title: Amend 'Save and return' keeps required checks in plants but skips them in animals
killed.what: Plants kit only gives isHubExit, so every plants page passes `allowMissing: kit.isHubExit(request)`. Only 'Save and return to overview' skips required-answer checks. The animals copy of kit.js also has amendReviewTarget/skipsRequiredChecks (added by animals fa115bd6, 'soft-save as Design Release 2.1 does'). That also treats an amend 'Save and return' to the review (?change=1) as a soft save, in line with the prototype source the journey-foundation backlog cites ('app/routes.js:1560-1566 (hub and review are soft-save actions)'). So the same amend control behaves differently in the two duplicated frontends. Only import-reason uses it in animals, so this may be deliberate scope. But plants has no equivalent and no recorded decision either way.
killed.scenario: A trader amends a submitted plants notification, opens Arrival details from the overview, clears the arrival time and presses 'Save and return'. The plants page refuses it with the required-time error. In animals, the equivalent amend 'Save and return' on Main reason for import with a follow-up left blank saves and goes to the amend review.
killed.fix: Decide whether an amend 'Save and return' is a soft save in plants. If it is, port skipsRequiredChecks into plants kit.js and use it in place of isHubExit in the plants controllers that pass allowMissing. If it is not, record the decision beside ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm so the two copies are known to differ on purpose.
killed.refutation: The facts are right. Plants kit.js has only isHubExit (line 126). arrival-details/controller.js:192 and the other plants pages pass `allowMissing: kit.isHubExit(request)`, and their templates use amendFormActions. So on plants, an amend 'Save and return' (?change=1) with a required answer blank is refused. But that is the plants increment working as scoped, not a shared-code defect. journey-foundation inc-003 (plans/inc-003.md) scopes soft save to 'Save and return to overview' only, and its AC5 for plants proves exactly that. Animals' skipsRequiredChecks came from a separate per-page increment (fa115bd6, inc-022, commodities-and-reason theme) and is used only on import-reason. Every other animals page also refuses a blank on amend 'Save and return', so the gap is within animals as well as between the two frontends, not a plants regression. It is worth one line to Sam as an open product question (the prototype treats the review as a soft-save action), but it is not a defect in the changed shared code.

results.title: INS frontend
results.summary: I reviewed the whole trade-imports-ins-frontend diff from origin/main to HEAD (7 commits, 26 files). The page-title change follows the GOV.UK pattern in both English and Welsh, and its tests are sound. The SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED link matches inc-113 and the animals backend's status enum. The countries stub now loads from a captured fixture, and GB is still added by address-countries.js. The capture script is a harmless dev script. The real problem is errors.js. Its cause-chain logging logs no secrets or personal data, but it misses most of the failures it was written to explain. Two weaker points remain: a cause chain with no end, and a raw status enum shown to users.
results.answers:
Can errors.js log personal data or secrets? Not that I found. Each cause line is cause.stack (the error message and call frames) or String(cause). In this repo only two call sites set a cause, get-oidc-config-with-retry.js:20 and countries/index.js:19, and both pass an Error. Undici fetch, socket and timeout errors name host:port at most, never headers, tokens or request bodies. ProxyAgent errors do not include the HTTP_PROXY URL. A non-Error object cause would print as '[object Object]', not its fields. The risk is that a future cause holding a string payload would be logged word for word. The problems I found are that it misses most fetch failures (f1, f2) and can loop forever (f3), not leakage.

Page titles: layout.njk now renders '[Error: ]Page - Service - GOV.UK'. The Welsh copy also uses 'GOV.UK', which is correct. The unit tests and page-title.fit.spec.js cover the home page, the address book, the error prefix and the 404 page. Clean.

SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED link: matches plan inc-113. The status really reaches ins-backend (animals-backend ExchangedDocument sends status.name() as notificationStatusCode, which NotificationUpsertService stores). Animals-frontend's notification-view accepts it. Clean, apart from the display label (f4).

Countries stub from captured fixture: the fixture has no GB, but address-countries.js puts GB first itself, so address forms are unaffected. The stub notifications use FR, IE, DE and GB. GB has no entry in the fixture, so the dashboard falls back to the code 'GB' for that row in stub mode only (it already did for unknown codes). Minor.

scripts/capture-reference-data.js: a local dev script. It defaults to localhost:8086, uses no proxy (correct off CDP), sets exitCode on failure and writes whatever JSON comes back. It is never imported at runtime. Clean.
results.answersCheck: I agree that errors.js logs no secrets or personal data. Only two cause producers exist in the repo: get-oidc-config-with-retry.js and countries/index.js. The countries one puts its cause in Boom's data, which errors.js never reads, so in practice only undici errors and OIDC errors reach the logger. Neither carries headers, tokens or the HTTP_PROXY URL. I disagree with one detail in f1. The reviewer says the test's Boom.boomify(TypeError with cause) shape is one 'this code path never produces'. That is true for the countries path, but hapi boomifies any uncaught error thrown from a handler in exactly that way. So stackWithCauses does work for uncaught fetch failures, and the gap is narrower than the summary ('misses most of the failures') implies. The failures it does miss are the countries 503 (f1) and every controller-caught error (f2). The other clean calls hold: page titles, the SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED link mapping, the GB handling in the stub fixture and the capture script. I would not count the raw-status label (f4) against this build, because inc-113 explicitly defers it to the theme that owns dashboard copy.

survived.title: Countries 503 still logs no fetch cause: Boom puts the cause in data, not error.cause
survived.what: stackWithCauses follows error.cause. The only 5xx Boom this app raises around a fetch is Boom.serverUnavailable('Reference data unavailable', { dataset, cause: err }). @hapi/boom has no cause option, so the fetch error goes into response.data.cause and response.cause stays undefined. catchAll then logs only the Boom stack. The new test builds Boom.boomify(new TypeError('fetch failed', { cause })), a shape this code path never produces.
survived.scenario: On CDP, reference-data is unreachable (for example the egress proxy or DNS fails) → GET /address-book/add → ensureLoaded throws Boom 503 → catchAll logs 'Error: Reference data unavailable' and its stack, with no 'Caused by:' line. The socket or DNS error this commit was meant to expose is still missing from the log.
survived.fix: Use Boom.boomify(err, { statusCode: 503, message: 'Reference data unavailable', data: { dataset: 'countries' } }), which keeps the original error and its cause chain. Or attach the cause to the Boom (Object.assign(boom, { cause: err })). Add a test that drives ensureLoaded with nock replyWithError and checks the logged 'Caused by:' line.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed. countries/index.js:17 (untouched by the diff, but it is the main 5xx path the new errors.js logging is for) calls Boom.serverUnavailable(message, data). @hapi/boom 'serverUnavailable(message, data)' passes data through internals.serverError to options.data (lib/index.js:117-118, 381-383), and boom never sets err.cause, so response.cause is undefined. The dashboard controller rethrows Boom errors (controller.js:114-115), so an unreachable reference-data service reaches catchAll as a 503 and stackWithCauses prints only the Boom stack, with no 'Caused by:'. One correction: the test shape (Boom.boomify of a TypeError with a cause) is not impossible. It is exactly what hapi does to an uncaught non-Boom error thrown from a handler, so the new code does work for uncaught throws. It does not work for the countries outage, which is the one fetch path this app wraps in Boom itself. Fix as suggested: boomify the original error with statusCode 503, or keep the cause on the Boom.

survived.title: Controller catch blocks still log fetch failures without their causes
survived.what: The commit says it fixes 'A 500 from a failed backend call logged only TypeError: fetch failed'. But the dashboard and every address-book controller catch non-Boom errors themselves, log them with logger.error({ err }, ...) and return a 500 view. Those errors never reach catchAll. The logger uses @elastic/ecs-pino-format, whose error formatter writes only err.stack as error.stack_trace (checked in node_modules/@elastic/ecs-helpers/lib/error-formatters.js), so the causes are still dropped there.
survived.scenario: ins-backend times out → GET / → listNotifications rejects with TypeError('fetch failed', { cause: ConnectTimeoutError }) → dashboard/controller.js:117 logs { err } → the ECS line holds only 'TypeError: fetch failed', with no host or connect-timeout detail. This is the same diagnostic gap the commit claims to close.
survived.fix: Add the causes at the logger instead of in catchAll. For example, add a pino err serializer or formatter in logger-options.js that writes stackWithCauses(err) into error.stack_trace. Then catchAll can log { err: response } like every other call site, which also follows the pino-logging best practice of always logging { err }.
survived.verifierNote: Factually right. Every controller catch block logs logger.error({ err }, ...) (dashboard/controller.js:117, add/edit/delete/list/view controllers). @elastic/ecs-helpers formatError writes only err.stack into error.stack_trace, and logger-options.js adds no err serializer, so causes are dropped there and those errors never reach catchAll. The commit message ('A 500 from a failed backend call logged only TypeError: fetch failed') therefore claims more than it fixes. Severity lowered to low: the catch blocks predate the diff, nothing regressed, and the gap only costs diagnostics. The dashboard path renders a recoverable-error view rather than a 500. Moving cause handling into a pino err serializer is the right fix and would also cover f1's catchAll path.

survived.title: Fixture test asserts static data, and the exact count breaks on every recapture
survived.what: fixtures.test.js checks the contents of a checked-in JSON file: 249 entries, AF first, Aland Islands second, JE present. No app behaviour is tested. The test only fails when someone runs npm run capture:reference-data and MDM has changed, which is the refresh the script exists for.
survived.scenario: MDM adds or renames a country → a developer recaptures → toHaveLength(249) or the order assertions fail, and the test gets 'fixed' by editing the numbers. The test protects nothing.
survived.fix: Delete the count and order assertions. If a guard is wanted, keep one shape check (an array of { code, name } with no GB). The behaviour is already covered by run-mode.test.js and the address-book tests.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed. fixtures.test.js imports a checked-in JSON file and asserts its length (249), its first two entries and that JE is present. It tests no app behaviour and fails only on a legitimate recapture, which conflicts with Sam's no-coverage-padding and test-behaviour rules. The 'no GB' assertion has some value as a guard, since address-countries.js adds GB itself and a GB in the fixture would duplicate it. Keep that check plus a { code, name } shape check, and drop the count and order assertions.

killed.title: stackWithCauses loops forever on a cause chain that cycles
killed.what: while (cause) { ... cause = cause.cause } has no record of causes already seen and no depth limit. pino-std-serializers' own stackWithCauses guards against cycles for exactly this reason.
killed.scenario: Any error whose cause chain loops (a.cause = b; b.cause = a, or err.cause = err, which some retry or wrapping code produces) reaches catchAll as a 5xx → the loop never ends and the lines array keeps growing. The request hangs, then the process blocks the event loop and runs out of memory, taking every user on that instance with it.
killed.fix: Track the causes already seen in a Set and stop on a repeat, or cap the depth, matching pino-std-serializers' err-helpers.
killed.refutation: The missing cycle guard is real in principle, but I found nothing that can produce a cyclic cause. The only cause producers are undici fetch errors (a linear chain), get-oidc-config-with-retry.js and countries/index.js, which puts its cause in data so the loop never sees it. No retry or wrapping code here assigns err.cause back up the chain. It is a hardening suggestion, not a demonstrable defect. Adding a Set guard is cheap if someone is already changing the function.

killed.title: New status shown to users as the raw enum 'SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED'
killed.what: mapNotificationRows passes notification.status through to the table cell unchanged. Older statuses already showed as raw enums, but this one adds an upper-case underscored token to a user-facing GOV.UK page. The animals frontend labels the same status 'Submitted action required' (shared/kit.js). The new fit test asserts the raw cell text, which locks the enum in.
killed.scenario: A trader has a notification submitted without its health certificate → the INS dashboard shows 'SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED' in the Status column, while the live-animals pages for the same notification show a 'Submitted action required' tag.
killed.fix: Map status to a copy label (and a govukTag) in the dashboard view-model, in English and Welsh, as the animals frontend does. Then make the fit test assert the label. This may need its own increment, because the older statuses have the same gap.
killed.refutation: list.js:112 is not touched by the diff, and every status already shows as its raw code. inc-113's plan decides this deliberately (decision 12: 'The status cell keeps printing the raw code, as it does for every status today. The dashboard template and copy belong to another theme'), and its out-of-scope list repeats it. survived.title: Transit and destination subdivision codes go to GBN-AG as country codes
survived.what: offeredCountries now returns countries.destinationCountryOptions(), which includes subdivisions such as ES-CN. Validation accepts these codes and the controller saves them into transitedCountries; import-reason's destination selects do the same. survived.title: Outstanding-row error links trap a half-done row in a Check your answers loop
survived.what: outstandingRowHref sends every row error to rowEntry(row) (the row's FIRST gate-passing page) wrapped in withChange (?change=1). The pages post back to their own URL (form has no action), and kit.exitTarget turns any ?change=1 save into a redirect to notification-view. When the row is outstanding because a LATER page in it is unanswered, the trader is sent to the first page, which is already answered. Saving there returns them to Check your answers with the same error, and the page that is actually missing is never reached.
survived.scenario: Plants-for-planting draft with arrivalStatus = not-yet-arrived and no arrivalDate (or a potatoes draft with commodityType set but no commodity lines). Continue on Check your answers gives 'Complete arrival details' (or 'Complete what you are importing'). The link opens /arrival-status?change=1 (or /commodity-type?change=1) with the radio already checked. Save and continue: arrival-status always calls nextTarget, which goes back to /notification-view. commodity-type does the same when no lines are removed. The same error shows again, so the trader loops until they find another way in through Overview. The fit test only covers potatoes, where arrival-status is out of scope, so it misses this. controller.test.js asserts href `${base}/commodity-type?change=1`, which fixes the defect in place.
survived.fix: Link each row error to the first gate-passing page in the row whose collects are not yet fulfilled (use statusOf per page), not to the row's first page. Or keep the change context only for single-page rows and send multi-page rows to the hub row entry without ?change=1. Add a plants/wood test for the arrival row (status answered, date missing) and a test for a typed commodity row with no lines.

ranked.headline: Start with the animals backend. It now sends the status SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED to PIMS on events whose published schemas allow only SUBMITTED, and that is the one high-severity finding. Next, in the same area, look at the cancel-amend status that can disagree with the documents held. Then look at the plants confirmation date, which is wrong by a day for the first hour after midnight in summer because the backend saves a time with no time zone. The tests were widened to accept the wrong day, so they hide it. Third, the workspace build gate, which can take down the stack and delete the lease that the run itself holds. In the frontends, begin with the backend fetch timeout and retry change. It does nothing useful on CDP, splits backend calls across two fetch paths, and only the local test paths exercise it. The same area also covers the raised FIT timeout. Then check that subdivision codes picked as transit countries reach GBN-AG as raw country codes, that the INS frontend still drops fetch causes from its logs, and that the plants Check your answers links send a trader round in a loop. The remaining findings are low severity: test strength, stub provenance, build-loop edge cases, comments and accessibility.

reviewOrder.why: It holds the only high-severity finding, a status value that breaks the published GBN-AG contract to PIMS, plus a stale-status defect on cancel-amend.
Its date checks were widened to hide a live one-day-off product bug, and several other assertions are looser than they should be.
The build gate can delete the run's own stack lease after Docker Desktop restarts, which affects lease safety and run continuity.
The k6 walk drifts slightly from the real opening run and logs a failure line, including the sign-in callback URL, on every iteration.
The code is sound; what remains is fixture provenance, overclaimed stub fidelity and test hygiene.
It must head the frontend list: the change does nothing on CDP, forks the fetch path, is tested through a library mock, and sits beside a raised FIT timeout.
Subdivision codes now chosen as transit and destination countries reach GBN-AG unmapped, and amend Save and return behaves differently from page to page.
The new cause logging misses the countries 503 and every error caught inside a controller, so the diagnostic gap it set out to close is still open.
It repeats the subdivision-to-GBN-AG risk and adds smaller contradictions in titles, accessibility and comments.
Check your answers error links can trap a trader in a loop, and a Welsh date, a cross-feature import and comment hygiene are open.

findings.title: SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED sent to PIMS on events whose schemas require SUBMITTED
findings.what: submitNotification and cancelAmendNotification now write the aggregate with status SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED. OutboxService then serialises it unchanged into two places: data.exchangedDocument.notificationStatusCode (through ExchangedDocument.from, status.name()) and statusChanges[].status. The events are NotificationSubmitted, NotificationSubmissionAmended and NotificationAmendmentCancelled, and each carries a schemaUrl. The schemas those URLs name all pin the value with {"const": "SUBMITTED"}: trade-imports-schemas gbn-ag-event-notification-submitted-v1, -submission-amended-v1 and -amendment-cancelled-v1. The GBN-AG status codelist (codelists/gbn-ag-notification-status.json) and gbn-ag-state-transitions.md know only DRAFT, SUBMITTED, AMEND and DELETED. trade-imports-schemas is still on main and has no change for the new status. The dynamics gateway passes the string straight through to PIMS (PimsGbnAgDataMapper/V2 pass doc.notificationStatusCode() through; OutboxStatusChange.status is a String). Sam's add-only ruling (claim 42) mapped the new status in the animals frontend and the INS frontend, but not in the external GBN-AG/PIMS contract. NotificationIT line 938 now pins the non-conforming value as expected behaviour, and four older outbox ITs were changed from SUBMITTED to SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED.
findings.scenario: A trader submits a live-animals notification without a scanned ITAHC. The ITs show this is now the default for any notification with no document. The outbox writes a NotificationSubmitted event that declares schemaUrl gbn-ag-event-notification-submitted-v1.schema.json but carries notificationStatusCode "SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED". The gateway forwards it to PIMS over Azure Service Bus. PIMS either fails schema validation, or does not recognise the code and does not treat the notification as submitted. The BCP and caseworkers then never see a pre-notification the trader believes was submitted. Each later amend, cancel-amend or resubmit repeats the problem.
findings.fix: Do not ship until the wire contract is settled. Option 1: keep the GBN-AG wire status as SUBMITTED by mapping SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED to SUBMITTED in ExchangedDocument.from and when building StatusChange. Carry the outstanding items as their own field if downstream needs them; this also means the INS backend (NotificationUpsertService reads status only from notificationStatusCode) needs another way to show 'action required'. Option 2: add the code to the gbn-ag codelist and minted v2 event schemas in trade-imports-schemas, agreed with the PIMS team, on the same branch name. Either way, add an IT asserting a clean-ITAHC submit's event carries notificationStatusCode SUBMITTED.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed on the branch. NotificationStatus gains SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED (diff). submitNotification (NotificationService.java:202-212) uses it whenever OutstandingItem.outstandingFor finds no COMPLETE ITAHC or HEALTH_CERTIFICATE. That covers no upload and also an ITAHC whose scan is still PENDING at submit. cancelAmendNotification (line 288) can restore it too. ExchangedDocument.from (outbox/gbnag/ExchangedDocument.java:32) writes status.name() into notificationStatusCode, and OutboxService:74-76 appends it to statusChanges. OutboxEventType points the schemaUrl at gbn-ag-event-notification-submitted-v1, -submission-amended-v1 and -amendment-cancelled-v1. In trade-imports-schemas all three pin exchangedDocument.notificationStatusCode to {"const": "SUBMITTED"} (checked submitted-v1 line 26), and that repo has no commits on the branch. The dynamics gateway's PimsGbnAgDataMapper and PimsGbnAgDataMapperV2 pass the string through unchanged. Sam's ruling claim 42 lists only the animals frontend, the INS frontend and the stub. His earlier ruling (point 8, 2026-10-09) says no PIMS profile or schema change is made in this programme. So the new value contradicts the declared contract and the stated scope. NotificationIT:938 pins the non-conforming value as correct. Whether PIMS actually rejects the event is unproven, but sending it breaches the declared contract, so high stands.

findings.title: Cancel-amend restores a stale outstanding-items status while document changes made during the amendment stay
findings.what: cancelAmendNotification sets the status from the outstandingItems kept from the last submission. Accompanying documents live in their own collection: an upload made during the amendment is not rolled back on cancel, and a deletion (DocumentService.deleteByUploadId, a hard delete) is not restored. Only notification content and fulfilments are restored. The restored status can therefore contradict the documents the notification holds, and the documents the AmendmentCancelled event lists in referenceDocument (OutboxService reads the live COMPLETE documents). The designed path for clearing 'action required' is Continue, which starts an amendment (inc-113, c-144), so traders will take this path.
findings.scenario: Case A. A notification is SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED. The trader clicks Continue (amend), uploads an ITAHC that scans COMPLETE, then clicks Cancel amend. The status reverts to SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED and the dashboard warns that the certificate is missing, while the event's referenceDocument lists the clean ITAHC. Case B. A notification is SUBMITTED with an ITAHC. The trader amends, deletes the ITAHC, then cancels. The status becomes SUBMITTED with outstandingItems [], but no health certificate exists, and PIMS receives SUBMITTED with no ITAHC reference.
findings.fix: Recompute on cancel as submit does: OutstandingItem.outstandingFor(documentService.findByNotificationRef(referenceNumber)), then set both outstandingItems and the status from that result. Alternatively, snapshot the accompanying-document set at amend and restore it on cancel. Add an IT for the amend, upload ITAHC, cancel-amend path.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. cancelAmendNotification (line 288) takes the status from the outstandingItems stored at the last submit and never re-reads the documents. Nothing under accompanyingdocument/ mentions amend or cancel, and uploads and deletes have no notification-status guard. So documents added or removed during an amendment survive a cancel, while the status reverts. Meanwhile OutboxService:91 lists the live COMPLETE documents in the event. Case A is the realistic one: the designed recovery is amend, upload the ITAHC, then submit, and a trader who uploads and then cancels stays at action-required with a clean ITAHC on file. The documents not rolling back is older behaviour. The stale status that contradicts them is new in this diff. Medium is right.

findings.title: Date checks accept yesterday at any hour, hiding an off-by-one-day bug
findings.what: Commit 3e7b227 widened the plants confirmation 'Date of notification' check to accept yesterday, today or tomorrow. The animals view's 'Date created' and 'Date submitted' checks (notification-view-states.spec.ts:40, 183, 266) and the plants ones (review.spec.ts:412, 629) accept yesterday or today. The commit says the extra day is only needed in the hour after midnight BST, but the tests accept it at every hour of the day. The plants backend stores submittedAt as a LocalDateTime with no zone (NotificationAggregate.java:50), and the confirmation controller reads it with new Date(value) before formatting for Europe/London. The date shown is therefore only right when the frontend process runs in UTC, and the tests cannot catch it being wrong.
findings.scenario: The plants frontend runs with TZ=Europe/London (native dev, or a container setting changes). At 14:00 a trader submits on 12 October. The zone-less submittedAt is read as London time, so a UTC-to-London regression can push the date a day off. If the page shows 11 October, review.spec.ts:201 and :412 still pass because yesterday is in the accepted set. The same applies to the animals 'Date submitted' header.
findings.fix: Accept the previous day only when the London clock is between 00:00 and 01:00 (compute the expected set from the current time), or read submittedAt back through the API and format it in Europe/London to get one expected string. Separately, raise a ticket for the plants backend to serialise submittedAt as an Instant (or with an offset) so the frontend's new Date() does not depend on the process timezone.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. review.spec.ts:201 accepts -1/0/+1 days and :412, :629, plus notification-view-states.spec.ts:40, 183, 266, accept -1/0. Commit 3e7b227 says the extra day is only needed in the hour after midnight BST, but the tests accept it at every hour. The reviewer's scenario understates the problem: the bug is live, not hypothetical. The plants frontend Dockerfile already sets ENV TZ="Europe/London" (Dockerfile:9, :34). The backend stamps submittedAt with zone-less LocalDateTime.now() (NotificationService.java:236, NotificationAggregate.java:50), and confirmation/controller.js:25 parses it with new Date(value). A zone-less ISO date-time is parsed as process-local (London) time, so the page shows the backend JVM's UTC wall date. Between 00:00 and 01:00 BST it shows yesterday. The build widened the test to hide a real product bug, and the controller's own comment ('submittedAt is a UTC instant') is wrong. Fix: serialise submittedAt and created as an Instant or with an offset (or parse with an explicit Z), then tighten the tests to today only, or to a set computed from the London clock.

findings.title: Gate tears down and deletes the run's own lease after Docker Desktop quits
findings.what: psStackWithDocker (tim/src/exec/stack.js:159) now starts Docker Desktop again whenever docker ps says the daemon is unreachable. In the gate, takeLease calls acquireStack as RUN_HOLDER. The run's lease is state UP, and Docker came back with no containers (the stack sets no restart policies). So acquireDecision returns 'start', startUnderLease rebuilds the stack, and lease.started is true. runE2e's finally block then calls giveBack, and releaseStack runs stop-stack.sh and removes the lease file. The gate cannot tell 'I started a free stack' apart from 'I restarted my own run's stack'. Before this change, an unreachable daemon made takeLease fail. The stage reported it, and the new recoverDownStack in the loop would have taken the lease again.
findings.scenario: An overnight branch run holds the lease as ibl-…, and a Homebrew cask upgrade quits Docker Desktop. The ladder's `tim build gate --phase e2e --holder ibl-…` starts Docker, rebuilds the stack, runs the e2e rungs green, then stops the stack and deletes the lease. The next stage runs `tim docker lease status`: lease null, up false. By RUN_STACK_RULE that means stackHeld with holder null, and confirmStackHeld believes it (null !== RUN_HOLDER). The run stops as 'stack-held' and preserves the attempt; or, where no stage checks, every later e2e gate cold-starts the stack and tears it down. Between gates the stack has no lease, so another session can take it. The end-of-run release finds nothing to release. The stackDown → recoverDownStack path only fires when a stage reads the lease before any gate has 'healed' it.
findings.fix: Make acquireStack return whether the start replaced the holder's own lease (previous?.holder === holder), and have runE2e give the stack back only when the gate took a lease nobody held before (lease.started && !lease.resumedOwnLease). Add a gate test: own UP lease, Docker quit, e2e runs, then assert the lease is still the holder's and the stack is up.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed on the branch. The ladder's e2e gate runs with --holder RUN_HOLDER (increment-build-loop.js:945). takeLease (gate.js:259) calls acquireStack, and stackStatus now goes through psStackWithDocker (stack.js:159), which reopens Docker Desktop instead of throwing. The compose files under docker/stack set no `restart:` policy, so the stack comes back with no containers. acquireDecision (stack-lease.js:146) then returns 'start' for the holder's own UP lease when up is false. startUnderLease returns started:true, gate.js:429 calls giveBack, and releaseStack runs stop-stack.sh and removes the lease file. stack-lease.js and gate.js's lease logic are unchanged in the diff. Before the diff, though, the daemon-down case threw inside takeLease ('Can't tell whether the workspace stack is free') and never reached this path, so the diff is what makes it reachable. Unit and FIT gate phases' port checks now reopen Docker too, so the ladder's e2e gate is usually the first thing to see the down stack. recoverDownStack only runs if a stage reads the lease first. After that, a stage sees lease null and stops as stack-held (confirmStackHeld treats a null holder as not this run's), or every later e2e gate cold-starts and releases the stack. Medium is right: it costs lease safety and run continuity, but no wrong code lands green. Suggested fix: carry 'restarted own lease' from acquireStack and skip giveBack in that case.

findings.title: Two divergent HTTP paths; the CDP path is no longer exercised by any test environment
findings.what: connectBoundedDispatcher() returns undefined whenever HTTP_PROXY is set, so fetchOnce (line 58) splits behaviour by environment. Unit, FIT and the local E2E stack (no HTTP_PROXY: docker/stack sets none) send through npm undici 8.11.2's fetch, with an undici FormData copy and a private Agent. CDP, which injects HTTP_PROXY, sends through Node's built-in fetch, with Node's FormData, through the global ProxyAgent. The comment at lines 17-20 says the fork is needed because built-in fetch 'rejects' npm undici agents. The pre-fix logs show otherwise. inc-109-ladder-e2e-rerun at 20:13Z, before 19a76c54 at 20:26Z, shows built-in fetch already connecting through /home/node/node_modules/undici/lib/core/connect.js with a 10000ms timeout. This is because npm undici's lib/global.js installs its Agent under both 'undici.globalDispatcher.2' and, wrapped in a Dispatcher1Wrapper, the legacy '.1' symbol. So the parallel fetch was never needed. In CDP the change adds nothing: there is no 2s bound, and the retry fires only if the socket to the squid proxy itself fails. A backend the proxy cannot reach comes back as a 502/503 response (http target) or as RequestAbortedError 'Proxy response (503) !== 200 when HTTP Tunneling' (https target), and neither is in CONNECT_ERROR_CODES.
findings.scenario: A future change to how bodies or headers are built (another FormData field, a stream body, a Blob subclass) passes unit, FIT and local E2E because all of them take the undici path, then breaks only in CDP on the built-in fetch path. The reverse has already happened: 19a76c54 sent every upload as text/plain on the undici path, and the backend refused it with HttpMediaTypeNotSupportedException. d66b1dce had to patch that in, and only the E2E baseline caught it.
findings.fix: Revert backendFetch to `countBackendCall(); return fetch(url, init)`, and drop asUndiciFormData/forUndici and test/setup-backend-fetch.js. If a local connect bound is still wanted, set it in one place without forking fetch: for example, in setup-proxy's no-proxy branch call `setGlobalDispatcher(new Agent({ connect: { timeout } }))` from npm undici, which built-in fetch already honours through the legacy symbol. Gate it behind a stack-only env var, so CDP and the tests run the same fetch and FormData.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. backend-fetch.js:21-26 returns no dispatcher when httpProxy is set, so fetchOnce (line 58) sends CDP calls through built-in fetch, Node FormData and the global ProxyAgent, while unit, FIT and the local stack go through npm undici fetch, an undici FormData copy and a private Agent. The fork was not needed. npm undici's lib/global.js installs its Agent under 'undici.globalDispatcher.2' and also, wrapped in Dispatcher1Wrapper, under the legacy '.1' symbol. The pre-fix log inc-109-ladder-e2e-rerun (20:13:49Z) shows built-in fetch failing inside /home/node/node_modules/undici/lib/core/connect.js with 'timeout: 10000ms'. So setGlobalDispatcher(new Agent({connect:{timeout}})) in a stack-only branch would have bounded the connect without a second fetch path. findings.title: Transit and destination lists now offer subdivision codes that reach GBN-AG as raw country IDs
findings.what: destinationCountryOptions() (via countryAndSubdivisionOptions) now offers subdivision codes such as FR-MQ or PT-30 as values, and the transit country search and the import-reason destination select now take their allow-list from it. Origin handles subdivisions in two fields: countryOfOriginSubdivisionCode, mapped by notification-mapper/mapper-a/sections/origin.js to parentCountryCode(code) plus countrySubdivisionCode. Transit has no such split. mapper-a/sections/transport.js sends transitedCountries through unchanged. The backend's SpecifiedConsignment then builds TradeCountry.fromCountryCodes(transport.getTransitedCountries()), which wraps each string as CodedValue.of(code), so the GBN-AG TradeCountry ID becomes 'FR-MQ' instead of an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Sam's ruling (2026-10-09, items 26-27) says to offer the subdivisions, but neither inc-006 nor inc-174 looked at the outbound mapping. The inc-006 plan only checked that the backend's destinationCountry is a free string.
findings.scenario: A trader on a road consignment searches 'Martinique', picks 'Martinique (France)' and submits. The notification stores transitedCountries ['FR-MQ']. The animals backend outbox puts SpecifiedConsignment.transitCountries [{ID: 'FR-MQ'}] in the GBN-AG message. The downstream consumer rejects it or misreads the country, while the same territory chosen as the origin is sent correctly as FR plus subdivision FR-MQ.
findings.fix: Settle the contract before release. Either map transited and destination subdivisions the way origin does (parent country code, with the subdivision carried separately if GBN-AG has a field for it) in mapper-a/sections/transport.js and wherever destinationCountry leaves the service, or confirm with the GBN-AG/IPAFFS owners that subdivision codes are valid there. Add a mapper test for a subdivision transit code.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed on the branch. transit-countries/validate.js now builds offeredCodes and offeredCountries from countries.destinationCountryOptions(), which includes subdivision keys such as FR-MQ (countries/index.js countryAndSubdivisionOptions). Before this change transit used originCountries(), which held countries only. mapper-a/sections/transport.js:45 passes transitedCountries through as reader.scalar, and the diff leaves that file untouched. In the backend, TradeCountry.fromCountryCodes (outbox/gbnag/TradeCountry.java:21-27) wraps each string as CodedValue.of(code) with a null subdivision, and SpecifiedConsignment.java:43 sends that list. So a picked subdivision reaches GBN-AG as ID 'FR-MQ', while origin splits the same code into a parent country plus a subdivision. Nothing in the backend checks the codes. On destinationCountry: it goes through direct-fields.js and NotificationCopyMapper only, and I found no GBN-AG outbox use, so the release risk is mainly transit. Medium is right: it is a contract defect that the downstream consumer may reject, and no test covers it.

findings.title: Countries 503 still logs no fetch cause: Boom puts the cause in data, not error.cause
findings.what: stackWithCauses follows error.cause. The only 5xx Boom this app raises around a fetch is Boom.serverUnavailable('Reference data unavailable', { dataset, cause: err }). @hapi/boom has no cause option, so the fetch error goes into response.data.cause and response.cause stays undefined. catchAll then logs only the Boom stack. The new test builds Boom.boomify(new TypeError('fetch failed', { cause })), a shape this code path never produces.
findings.scenario: On CDP, reference-data is unreachable (for example the egress proxy or DNS fails) → GET /address-book/add → ensureLoaded throws Boom 503 → catchAll logs 'Error: Reference data unavailable' and its stack, with no 'Caused by:' line. The socket or DNS error this commit was meant to expose is still missing from the log.
findings.fix: Use Boom.boomify(err, { statusCode: 503, message: 'Reference data unavailable', data: { dataset: 'countries' } }), which keeps the original error and its cause chain. Or attach the cause to the Boom (Object.assign(boom, { cause: err })). Add a test that drives ensureLoaded with nock replyWithError and checks the logged 'Caused by:' line.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. countries/index.js:17 (untouched by the diff, but it is the main 5xx path the new errors.js logging is for) calls Boom.serverUnavailable(message, data). @hapi/boom 'serverUnavailable(message, data)' passes data through internals.serverError to options.data (lib/index.js:117-118, 381-383), and boom never sets err.cause, so response.cause is undefined. The dashboard controller rethrows Boom errors (controller.js:114-115), so an unreachable reference-data service reaches catchAll as a 503 and stackWithCauses prints only the Boom stack, with no 'Caused by:'. One correction: the test shape (Boom.boomify of a TypeError with a cause) is not impossible. It is exactly what hapi does to an uncaught non-Boom error thrown from a handler, so the new code does work for uncaught throws. It does not work for the countries outage, which is the one fetch path this app wraps in Boom itself. Fix as suggested: boomify the original error with statusCode 503, or keep the cause on the Boom.

findings.title: Transit and destination subdivision codes go to GBN-AG as country codes
findings.what: offeredCountries now returns countries.destinationCountryOptions(), which includes subdivisions such as ES-CN. Validation accepts these codes and the controller saves them into transitedCountries; import-reason's destination selects do the same. In the animals backend, SpecifiedConsignment builds the transit list with TradeCountry.fromCountryCodes(transport.getTransitedCountries()), which wraps each code unchanged as CodedValue.of(code). The origin page maps a subdivision back to its parent (parentCountryCode) for the region-code prefix, but nothing on the transit or destination path maps or splits a subdivision. The backlog deliberately asks for the subdivision code to be saved, but no increment checked what the outbound GBN-AG message does with it.
findings.scenario: A rail consignment adds 'Canary Islands (Spain)' as a transit country, so transitedCountries is ['ES-CN']. When submitted, the GBN-AG payload carries a TradeCountry with code ES-CN where an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code is expected. The downstream system may reject the message or mis-route it, and the frontend fit tests cannot see this.
findings.fix: Before merge, confirm with the GBN-AG/PIMS mapping (docs/analysis/gbn-ag-field-lineage.md) whether a subdivision code is valid in the transit and destination country fields. If it is not, map it to its parent (and send the subdivision separately if the schema has a slot for it) in the backend outbox mapper, not in the frontend. Add an outbox test with a subdivision code either way.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. transit-countries/validate.js now builds offeredCodes and offeredCountries from countries.destinationCountryOptions(), and the new unit test 'Should commit a subdivision code and continue' saves ['FR','ES-CN']. In the backend, TradeCountry.fromCountryCodes (outbox/gbnag/TradeCountry.java:21) wraps each code unchanged as new TradeCountry(CodedValue.of(code), null) and leaves the subordinateTradeCountrySubDivision slot it has empty. So ES-CN goes out as a country code. The backlog row (arrival-and-transit, 'Save and continue saves its code') asks for this on Sam's 9 Oct ruling, but no row checks the outbound GBN-AG message. One part of the claim is overstated: destinationCountry is not mapped into the gbnag outbox at all (no match in outbox/), so the GBN-AG risk is limited to transit countries. findings.title: Outstanding-row error links trap a half-done row in a Check your answers loop
findings.what: outstandingRowHref sends every row error to rowEntry(row) (the row's FIRST gate-passing page) wrapped in withChange (?change=1). The pages post back to their own URL (form has no action), and kit.exitTarget turns any ?change=1 save into a redirect to notification-view. When the row is outstanding because a LATER page in it is unanswered, the trader is sent to the first page, which is already answered. Saving there returns them to Check your answers with the same error, and the page that is actually missing is never reached.
findings.scenario: Plants-for-planting draft with arrivalStatus = not-yet-arrived and no arrivalDate (or a potatoes draft with commodityType set but no commodity lines). Continue on Check your answers gives 'Complete arrival details' (or 'Complete what you are importing'). The link opens /arrival-status?change=1 (or /commodity-type?change=1) with the radio already checked. Save and continue: arrival-status always calls nextTarget, which goes back to /notification-view. commodity-type does the same when no lines are removed. The same error shows again, so the trader loops until they find another way in through Overview. The fit test only covers potatoes, where arrival-status is out of scope, so it misses this. controller.test.js asserts href `${base}/commodity-type?change=1`, which fixes the defect in place.
findings.fix: Link each row error to the first gate-passing page in the row whose collects are not yet fulfilled (use statusOf per page), not to the row's first page. Or keep the change context only for single-page rows and send multi-page rows to the hub row entry without ?change=1. Add a plants/wood test for the arrival row (status answered, date missing) and a test for a typed commodity row with no lines.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed on the branch. outstanding-rows.js:45-48 is new. It links each row error to rowEntry(row) plus ?change=1, and rowEntry (flow/navigation.js:20-23) returns the row's first gate-passing page whatever has already been answered there. Both arrival-status and commodity-type have a form with no action (`<form method="post" novalidate>`), so the POST keeps ?change=1. kit.exitTarget (kit.js:133-137) then sends the trader to CYA_SLUG. arrival-status/controller.js always ends with nextTarget. commodity-type does the same unless lines were removed. The arrival row is [arrivalStatusPage, arrivalDetailsPage] and the commodities row is [commodityTypePage, commoditiesPage, commodityDetailsPage] (task-rows.js:30,33). So a row with its first page answered and a later page missing sends the trader to the answered page and straight back to Check your answers with the same error. controller.test.js:336-346 seeds potatoes with no lines and asserts href `${base}/commodity-type?change=1`, which is exactly this trap. The trader can still get out through Overview or a summary-row Change link, so it is a navigation loop, not data loss. Medium stands.

findings.title: No IT covers the path that clears action-required, or a clean submit's event
findings.what: The existing outbox event ITs (around lines 1340, 1444 and 1488) were re-pointed from SUBMITTED to SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED instead of being given a clean ITAHC, and their comments still say 'through SUBMITTED'. As a result, no integration test asserts the normal event a correct submit produces: a clean ITAHC giving notificationStatusCode SUBMITTED. No IT drives the designed recovery path either: SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED, then amend, upload a clean ITAHC, resubmit, then SUBMITTED with outstandingItems [] on the stored aggregate and the NotificationSubmissionAmended event. That path is unit-tested only, with DocumentService mocked.
findings.scenario: Suppose a regression makes resubmission ignore documents uploaded during an amendment, for example by reading documents for the wrong reference or reading before the upload is persisted. Every IT stays green, and traders are left stuck at 'Submitted action required' after uploading their certificate.
findings.fix: Add ITs through the real endpoints for both paths. First: submit, amend, givenACleanItahc, submit; assert status SUBMITTED, outstandingItems empty, and the last event's notificationStatusCode. Second: a clean-ITAHC first submit asserting the event's notificationStatusCode is SUBMITTED. Fix the stale 'through SUBMITTED' comments in the re-pointed tests.
findings.verifierNote: Partly overstated but real. A clean-ITAHC submit IT exists (NotificationIT:867), but it asserts only the aggregate status and outstandingItems. It does not check the outbox event's notificationStatusCode, and the only IT on that field is line 938, which pins SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED. No IT drives the path SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED, then amend, upload a clean ITAHC, resubmit. createAndSubmitNotificationWithFullContent seeds the ITAHC before the first submit. The stale comment at line 1341 ('through SUBMITTED') sits above an assertion of SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED, as the reviewer said. This is a test gap only, so low.

findings.title: Failed-attempt handler's soft reset sweeps up commits that are not the attempt's
findings.what: New step 0 of the branch-lifecycle preserve prompt treats every commit in `origin/<branch>..HEAD` as the failed attempt's work. It writes them out as a patch, then runs `reset --soft origin/<branch>`, and later steps stash the result. That rests on 'No stage commits: only landing does, and it pushes at once'. But the loop has a push-failed outcome that leaves a landed, recorded, unpushed commit on the branch by design ('a resume pushes the recorded commit'). The branch baseline (branchBaselinePrompt) never checks the ahead count, and a person's own unpushed commit on the theme branch also passes the clean-tree baseline.
findings.scenario: Row A lands, its push is rejected because the remote moved, and the run stops push-failed with A's commit SHA recorded. The person relaunches with an explicit id queue, or the derived order puts row B first. B's ladder goes red, and preserveAttempt soft-resets A's commit together with B's work into B's failure stash. A's row still records its commit, so A resumes past build. The find-PRs stage sees nothing ahead to push and marks A done. A's change never reaches the branch, and survives only in logs/<B>-preserve-*.commits.patch.
findings.fix: Either make the baseline refuse to start a row when any configured repo has commits ahead of origin/<branch> (or push them first, as the find-PRs stage does), or have step 0 reset only commits made after a HEAD SHA the loop records at the start of the row's baseline.
findings.verifierNote: Step 0 (increment-build-loop.js:1510-1517, added in 4d734946) does soft-reset everything in origin/<branch>..HEAD in every configured repo. The push-failed outcome (4363-4371) does leave a recorded, unpushed commit, and branchBaselinePrompt (2848) checks only the branch and clean trees, never the ahead count. So the scenario can happen. It needs three things: a push-failed stop, a relaunch before the human reconciles the branch (which the code comment expects them to do), and a different row's red ladder before A is pushed. A different row comes first only with an explicit id queue or a derived order that puts B first. Nothing is lost outright: the commits go to logs/<B>-preserve-*.commits.patch and the note names their SHAs. A's row would still show a commit that is not on the branch, though, which is a silent integrity gap. The scenario is narrow and the work can be recovered, so low rather than medium. The fix the reviewer suggests (refuse at baseline when ahead > 0, or record a per-row HEAD and reset only past it) is sound.

findings.title: Theme spec check stops the run on gaps that predate the theme, and on prefixes the theme never touched
findings.what: themeSpecCheck turns any `tim spec gaps --none` noneCount > 0, or any lint finding, across the whole prefix into a 'spec-check-red' stop. That includes gaps that predate the theme. It also adds every prefix reachable from the repos of theme rows this run did not build. A row with no `repos` counts as touching every configured repo, and animals-backend maps to both live-animals and germinal-products.
findings.scenario: A theme was built over two launches, and its earlier rows changed only trade-imports-animals-backend for live animals. When the last row lands, the 'repo reach' source adds germinal-products/. That prefix has unproven scenarios from before this programme, so the run stops with SPEC CHECK RED and prescribes 'catch-up and cover germinal' for a set the theme never touched.
findings.fix: Compare against a per-prefix gaps baseline taken at the run's (or theme's) first baseline and stop only on new noneScenarios. For rows not built in this run, use the prefixes recorded in their landed Spec sync lines, which are already parsed, instead of repo reach.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. prefixesBySource (3243-3250) adds 'repo reach' for rows this run did not build. SPEC_PREFIXES_BY_REPO_PATH (753-762) maps both animals repos to ['live-animals','germinal-products']. gapsProblem (3209) turns any noneCount > 0 into a problem, and themeSpecCheck stops the run with spec-check-red. A theme built over two launches can therefore stop on germinal-products gaps it never touched, and the run prescribes 'catch-up and cover germinal'. Stopping on gaps that predate the theme within prefixes the theme did touch is arguably the intended strict policy, given Sam's 'failures are mine to fix' stance. The repo-reach over-inclusion is the real defect. The effect is a false stop at the end of a theme with a clear message, not wrong code, so low. The better fix is to use the recorded landed Spec sync prefixes for rows not built in this run.

findings.title: FIT deny rule blocks only test:fit, not test:fit:features or test:fit:journeys
findings.what: FIT_ON_STACK_PORT = /\brun test:fit(?!:)/ is meant to refuse plan checks that serve a frontend on the stack's port. The negative lookahead lets any `test:fit:<suffix>` through. In animals-frontend and plants-frontend, `test:fit:features` and `test:fit:journeys` call `npm run test:fit` with no PORT, and playwright.config.js sets reuseExistingServer: false.
findings.scenario: A planner writes `npm --prefix ~/…/trade-imports-plants-frontend run test:fit:features -- tests/x.spec.js` as a section-5 check. The deny list accepts it, the webServer can't bind 3003 (the leased stack holds it), and the ladder goes red, preserving and stopping a correct increment.
findings.fix: Deny every test:fit form except test:fit:ci, e.g. /\brun test:fit(?!:ci\b)/, and add a contract test case for test:fit:features.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. FIT_ON_STACK_PORT = /\brun test:fit(?!:)/ (line 1364) lets test:fit:features and test:fit:journeys through. In both frontends these scripts call `npm run test:fit` with no PORT. plants playwright.config.js uses PORT ?? 3003 with reuseExistingServer: false, so on a leased stack holding that port the webServer cannot start. A planner who writes test:fit:features as a section-5 check gets past the deny list, and the ladder goes red with nothing broken. Low, because the effect is a false red stop, which preserves the work. The fix /\brun test:fit(?!:ci\b)/ plus a contract test is right.

findings.title: Read-only stack queries now launch Docker Desktop and can block for 5 minutes
findings.what: Every caller of stackContainers or stackContainerIds now goes through psStackWithDocker: lease status, gate held-port checks, writeStackLogs, recordLeaseContainers. On macOS that runs `open -a Docker` and polls for up to TIM_DOCKER_START_WAIT_MS (default 5 minutes) whenever the daemon is unreachable. On a machine whose docker context is Colima or OrbStack, the daemon-unreachable stderr matches but `open -a Docker` fails. The user then sees 'Docker Desktop would not open' instead of the real cause.
findings.scenario: Someone runs `tim docker lease status` to check who holds the stack while Docker is deliberately stopped. Docker Desktop opens and the command hangs for up to 5 minutes. withStackLogs after a red e2e rung can stall the same way.
findings.fix: Restart Docker only on the start paths (run-stack.sh and acquire). Let status reads report 'Docker not running' as up:false with a reason. Check `docker context show` before assuming Docker Desktop.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. stackStatus → stackContainerIds → psStackWithDocker → ensureDockerRunning (docker-daemon.js:81) runs `open -a Docker` and polls for up to TIM_DOCKER_START_WAIT_MS (5 minutes by default). So `tim docker lease status`, the gate's port checks and writeStackLogs all launch Docker Desktop as a side effect of a read. The 5-minute hang happens only when Desktop opens but never answers; a normal start takes well under a minute. The Colima and OrbStack case is real but hypothetical on this team, which runs Docker Desktop. It is a design wart rather than a breaking bug. It also feeds f1, because it makes the stack read heal the daemon silently. Low.

findings.title: Missed-dashboard warning is logged on every VU iteration and includes the OIDC callback URL with its auth code
findings.what: openInsDashboard calls console.warn(describeMissedPage(...)) on every failed dashboard check, on the hot path of dashboardOnlySession, addressBookSession and every journey session. Every other console call in src/k6 and src/suites runs in setup or teardown. describeMissedPage puts the full page.url in the line. The commit's own test shows this is the /auth/sign-in-oidc?code=... callback when sign-in fails.
findings.scenario: Defra ID or the INS session store degrades during a peak-day or spike run on CDP. Every dashboard-opening session, hundreds a minute, writes a warn line holding the authorisation code from the callback URL. The k6 log fills with near-identical lines and hides the setup and teardown summary lines. The codes end up in CDP's log store. They are short-lived and come from the stub, but it is a bad pattern to copy across to real identity providers.
findings.fix: Strip the query string before logging (pathOf in pages.js already does this). Log once per VU, or add to a Counter tagged with status and heading so the summary shows what the missed page was without one line per iteration.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed in src/k6/front-door.js:61-65. console.warn(describeMissedPage(...)) runs on every failed dashboard check inside openInsDashboard, which is on the per-session hot path. describeMissedPage puts in the full url, query string included, and the commit's own test case shows a /auth/sign-in-oidc?code=... URL. The reviewer is slightly overstated in saying every other console call is in setup or teardown: call-counts.js and resilience.js also log at run time. Still, nothing else logs once per iteration on a failure path. The code reaching the log has already been spent on the failed callback, and in perf it comes from the Defra ID stub, so the security risk is minimal. The flooding during a degraded run is real. Fix: strip the query with pathOf, and either log once per VU or count failures with a tagged Counter.

findings.title: k6 live-animals walk still out of step with the real opening run after additional-details; cph-number is no longer a run step
findings.what: The frontend's RUN_STEPS (animals-frontend src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js) now runs origin, commodities, import-reason, consignment-details, identification, additional-details, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, documents, addresses (endsRunWhenComplete), contact, notification-view. This change also removed cph-number from the run: it is reached only from its row on the addresses page. The k6 draft fixes only the first six steps. It still walks additional-details, documents, addresses, cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, contact. walker.reach (src/k6/pages.js) throws away the page a save landed on when its path differs from the next step's, and opens the expected page directly. The `saved` check only tests status 200, no stale redirect and no redirect loop. So every mismatch costs a GET a real user never makes, and nothing fails. The new live-animals.test.js claims the order is 'as Design Release 2.1 orders them' but pins only names.slice(0, 6), so the wrong tail is locked in, not caught.
findings.scenario: A single-session live-animals notification during peak-day. (1) The additional-details save lands on /port-of-entry; k6 discards it and GETs /documents. (2) The addresses save lands on /consignment/contact/select, or on the hub when nothing is outstanding; k6 GETs /cph-number, a page the run no longer visits. (3) The cph-number save falls through nextInTaskRow back to /addresses; k6 GETs /port-of-entry. (4) The transporters save lands on /documents; k6 GETs /consignment/contact/select. That is 4 extra page renders per notification, about 2 of them new since the opening-run change. Each is counted in page_requests and run.counter. reEditUntilTarget then cuts the padding re-edits to keep pagesPerNotification, so the per-endpoint mix (documents, cph-number, port-of-entry and contact GETs up, re-edit saves down) drifts from the traffic model. Every check stays green.
findings.fix: Reorder the draft tail to match RUN_STEPS: additional-details, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, documents, addresses, contact. Model cph-number as a detour inside the addresses step: open it from the addresses page, save it, land back on addresses, then save addresses. Drop it from its own top-level slot. Change live-animals.test.js to assert the full draft order. Better still, make reach record a counter or warn (reuse describeMissedPage) when, during the opening run, it has to open a page directly instead of landing on it, so the next frontend reorder fails loudly.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed on the branch. The animals-frontend diff to flow/run.js removes cphNumberPage from RUN_STEPS and adds endsRunWhenComplete on addresses. The k6 draft in src/k6/live-animals.js (lines 208-218) still walks documents, addresses, cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, contact. walker.reach in src/k6/pages.js:150 keeps the landed page only when the status is 200 and the path matches. Otherwise it opens the expected path directly, and saved() only checks isSaved. Mismatches therefore cost extra GETs and nothing fails. live-animals.test.js pins only names.slice(0, 6). I am downgrading it from medium. Most of the tail mismatch was already on main, since main's frontend also ran port-of-entry before documents. The only new drift is addresses → cph-number: main's run went from addresses to cph-number, and now it goes to contact. That is about one extra direct GET per notification. Real users still open cph-number from its row on the addresses page, so it stays a real page in the mix. Thresholds and measurements are unchanged, so this is a small skew in the traffic model, not a broken measurement. The suggested fix is sound: reorder the tail, make cph-number a detour from addresses, assert the full order, and warn or count when reach falls back mid-run.

findings.title: An unrecognised MDM traffic value silently becomes type null and sorts last
findings.what: fromTraffic matches 'Airport', 'Port' and 'Rail' exactly, ignoring case only. It does not trim, and no log or metric records a miss. PortOfEntry maps a miss to null, and PortListOrder puts null types after rail. Every observed value is one of the three, but only CDP-test MDM was captured, not production, and MDM's data is known to be messy (duplicates, 'Teestort', non-breaking spaces).
findings.scenario: Production MDM returns traffic 'Port ' (trailing space), 'Seaport', 'Sea Port' or 'Airport/Port' for a real port. reference-data serves it with "type":null after Folkestone, below every rail port. findings.title: ETIMEDOUT in the retry set is not guaranteed to mean the request was never sent
findings.what: The retry runs for every method, including POST /notifications (create), /{id}/copy, /{id}/submit, /amend, /soft-delete, /notifications/{id}/document-uploads and /document-uploads/{id}/file. It fires if any cause in the chain has UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, ECONNREFUSED or ETIMEDOUT. The first two can only happen before any request bytes are sent, including during the TLS handshake for an https target, so retrying on them is safe. ETIMEDOUT can also be raised on an established keep-alive socket, from a kernel keepalive or retransmission failure after the request has been written. The logs only show ETIMEDOUT nested under UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT (AggregateError from internalConnectMultiple), so it adds no coverage.
findings.scenario: POST /notifications/{id}/submit is written on a reused keep-alive socket and the backend commits it. The path then drops before the response arrives and the socket errors with ETIMEDOUT. backendFetch sends the submit again, and the second call gets a 409 or state error, or (on create or copy) a duplicate notification. Unlikely within undici's 300s headersTimeout, but possible, and nothing guards against it.
findings.fix: If the retry survives, limit CONNECT_ERROR_CODES to UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT and ECONNREFUSED, and preferably retry only GET/PUT/DELETE, or require an idempotency key for POST.
findings.verifierNote: ETIMEDOUT is in CONNECT_ERROR_CODES at line 14, and isConnectError walks the whole cause chain for every method, including POST submit, create and copy. undici's h1 client passes a socket error on an established socket straight to in-flight requests as the raw error, unless it is ECONNRESET at message end. So a kernel ETIMEDOUT after the request was written would be retried. The unit test at backend-fetch.test.js:110 shows the intent is not to resend once the connection has opened, and ETIMEDOUT contradicts that intent. It is rare and needs a mid-flight path drop. Low.

In the real-connection tests, test 1 passes with no agent and test 4 (line 104) asserts only the final ECONNREFUSED, so neither proves a second attempt. Nothing tests the 2s bound. The scenario overstates one point: deleting the retry branch at lines 74-78 WOULD fail backend-fetch.test.js:73-89, which drives the retry through the shim.
